Chapter 21 speaks of a historical catastrophe that will sweep over the whole land. When Jerusalem fell, faithful people suffered too. Jeremiah was dragged to Egypt. Daniel and Ezekiel were already exiles.

This is the world believers live in. God sends rain on the just and on the unjust (Matt 5:45), and disasters fall on both as well. Christians are not exempt from war, disease or collapse. But the same suffering has a different meaning for those who belong to God: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall tribulation, or distress... or sword?... No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us (Rom 8:35, 37).

Because I will cut off from you both righteous and wicked, therefore my sword shall be drawn from its sheath against all flesh from south to north.

And all flesh shall know that I am the LORD. I have drawn my sword from its sheath; it shall not be sheathed again.

It shall not be sheathed again — until its work is done. For years the sword stayed in its sheath while God warned. Now the warnings are over.

verseByVerse.quote: "As for you, son of man, groan; with breaking heart and bitter grief, groan before their eyes. And when they say to you, 'Why do you groan?' you shall say, 'Because of the news that it is coming. Every heart will melt, and all hands will be feeble; every spirit will faint, and all knees will be weak as water. Behold, it is coming, and it will be fulfilled,'" declares the Lord GOD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"As for you, son of man, groan; with breaking heart and bitter grief, groan before their eyes.

Ezekiel is not allowed to announce this calmly. He must groan... with breaking heart and bitter grief, publicly, before their eyes. The messenger's grief is part of the message.

And when they say to you, 'Why do you groan?' you shall say, 'Because of the news that it is coming. Every heart will melt, and all hands will be feeble; every spirit will faint, and all knees will be weak as water. Behold, it is coming, and it will be fulfilled,'" declares the Lord GOD.

People will ask, Why do you groan? And his answer: because I know what is coming. When the news of Jerusalem's fall arrives, every heart will melt and every knee will turn to water.

That is the posture of a faithful preacher of judgment. He does not stand at a distance, pointing. He groans. He feels the weight of what he announces. Jesus wept over Jerusalem before he foretold its fall. Anyone who can speak of God's judgment without a breaking heart has not yet understood it.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 8–17 — A Sword Sharpened and Polished
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: A sword, a sword is sharpened and also polished for slaughter (vv. 9-11). Ezekiel must cry out and strike his thigh, because it is against God's people and their princes, who despised the rod of discipline (vv. 10, 12-13). He claps his hands as the sword strikes again and again, flashing like lightning at every gate (vv. 14-16), and God himself claps his hands and satisfies his fury (v. 17).
verseByVerse.theology: Those who despise God's gentler discipline will meet his sword.

verseByVerse.quote: And the word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, prophesy and say, Thus says the Lord, say: "A sword, a sword is sharpened and also polished, sharpened for slaughter, polished to flash like lightning! (Or shall we rejoice? You have despised the rod, my son, with everything of wood.) So the sword is given to be polished, that it may be grasped in the hand. It is sharpened and polished to be given into the hand of the slayer. Cry out and wail, son of man, for it is against my people. It is against all the princes of Israel. They are delivered over to the sword with my people. Strike therefore upon your thigh. For it will not be a testing—what could it do if you despise the rod?" declares the Lord GOD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, prophesy and say, Thus says the Lord, say: "A sword, a sword is sharpened and also polished,

sharpened for slaughter, polished to flash like lightning! (Or shall we rejoice? You have despised the rod, my son, with everything of wood.)

This is a song of the sword — harsh, rhythmic, repetitive. A sword, a sword. Sharpened to cut, polished to flash. You can almost hear the blade on the whetstone.

The words in brackets are difficult. The ESV notes that its rendering is a probable reading, and the Hebrew is literally "The rod of my son despises everything of wood". But the sense seems clear enough: You have despised the rod, my son. The rod was the instrument of a father's discipline. My son, do not despise the LORD's discipline... for the LORD reproves him whom he loves, as a father the son in whom he delights (Prov 3:11-12). Israel had been disciplined with a rod again and again and had despised it. Now comes the sword.

That is a sobering principle. God's lighter discipline is a mercy meant to spare us heavier judgment. To ignore the rod is to invite the sword.

So the sword is given to be polished, that it may be grasped in the hand. It is sharpened and polished to be given into the hand of the slayer.

Cry out and wail, son of man, for it is against my people. It is against all the princes of Israel. They are delivered over to the sword with my people. Strike therefore upon your thigh.

It is against my people. That is what makes Ezekiel wail. Striking the thigh was a gesture of grief and horror.

For it will not be a testing—what could it do if you despise the rod?" declares the Lord GOD.

The ESV notes another possible reading: "For it is a testing; and what if even the rod despises? It shall not be!" The line is hard, but the thrust is plain: this sword is not another round of testing. It is the end of testing.

verseByVerse.quote: "As for you, son of man, prophesy. Clap your hands and let the sword come down twice, yes, three times, the sword for those to be slain. It is the sword for the great slaughter, which surrounds them, that their hearts may melt, and many stumble. At all their gates I have given the glittering sword. Ah, it is made like lightning; it is taken up for slaughter. Cut sharply to the right; set yourself to the left, wherever your face is directed. I also will clap my hands, and I will satisfy my fury; I the LORD have spoken."
verseByVerse.commentary:
"As for you, son of man, prophesy. Clap your hands and let the sword come down twice, yes, three times, the sword for those to be slain. It is the sword for the great slaughter, which surrounds them,

Ezekiel claps his hands as the sword swings — twice, yes, three times (the ESV notes, literally "its third"). The strokes keep coming. The sword surrounds them; there is no way out.

that their hearts may melt, and many stumble. At all their gates I have given the glittering sword. Ah, it is made like lightning; it is taken up for slaughter.

At all their gates — every entrance to the city will be guarded by the flashing sword. (The ESV notes that many stumble is literally "many stumbling blocks", and that the meaning of the word rendered taken up is uncertain.)

Cut sharply to the right; set yourself to the left, wherever your face is directed.

The sword is spoken to directly, like a living thing: strike right, strike left, wherever you turn.

I also will clap my hands, and I will satisfy my fury; I the LORD have spoken."

And then God himself claps his hands. This is not glee; it is the decisive signal that the verdict is given and the sentence will be carried out. His fury will be satisfied.

For those who shelter in Christ, the Bible's great news is that God's fury has already been satisfied — on the cross. The sword that was drawn against sinners was sheathed in the Shepherd: He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree (1 Pet 2:24).

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 18–27 — The King of Babylon at the Crossroads
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Ezekiel marks a signpost where the road forks — one way to Rabbah of the Ammonites, the other to Jerusalem (vv. 18-20). The king of Babylon stands at the fork and uses divination: arrows, household idols, a liver (v. 21). The lot for Jerusalem falls into his right hand (v. 22); the city thinks it is false, but its guilt is remembered (vv. 23-24). To the profane prince of Israel God says, Remove the turban and take off the crown (vv. 25-26). A ruin, ruin, ruin I will make it. This also shall not be, until he comes, the one to whom judgment belongs, and I will give it to him (v. 27).
verseByVerse.theology: God directs even pagan divination to accomplish his judgment, and he removes the crown until the rightful King comes.

verseByVerse.quote: The word of the LORD came to me again: "As for you, son of man, mark two ways for the sword of the king of Babylon to come. Both of them shall come from the same land. And make a signpost; make it at the head of the way to a city. Mark a way for the sword to come to Rabbah of the Ammonites and to Judah, into Jerusalem the fortified.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The word of the LORD came to me again:

"As for you, son of man, mark two ways for the sword of the king of Babylon to come. Both of them shall come from the same land. And make a signpost; make it at the head of the way to a city.

Mark a way for the sword to come to Rabbah of the Ammonites and to Judah, into Jerusalem the fortified.

Another sign. Ezekiel draws a road map, perhaps scratched in the dust, with a fork and a signpost. The Babylonian army is marching west. At some point the road divides. One branch leads to Rabbah, capital of Ammon, across the Jordan. The other leads to Jerusalem.

Both nations had rebelled against Babylon. Which will Nebuchadnezzar attack first? The exiles might have hoped for Rabbah. Ezekiel's map says: watch the signpost.

verseByVerse.quote: For the king of Babylon stands at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination. He shakes the arrows; he consults the teraphim; he looks at the liver. Into his right hand comes the divination for Jerusalem, to set battering rams, to open the mouth with murder, to lift up the voice with shouting, to set battering rams against the gates, to cast up mounds, to build siege towers. But to them it will seem like a false divination. They have sworn solemn oaths, but he brings their guilt to remembrance, that they may be taken.
verseByVerse.commentary:
For the king of Babylon stands at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination. He shakes the arrows; he consults the teraphim; he looks at the liver.

Picture the most powerful king in the world standing at a road junction, unable to decide, turning to his religious specialists. He shakes the arrows — marked arrows drawn from a quiver like lots. He consults the teraphim (the ESV notes, "household idols"). He looks at the liver — examining the liver of a sacrificed animal for omens.

It is superstition. And yet God controls the outcome. The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD (Prov 16:33). The king's heart is a stream of water in the hand of the LORD; he turns it wherever he will (Prov 21:1). Nebuchadnezzar thought his gods were guiding him. The LORD was.

There is comfort here. No human decision — by any king, government, or court — is outside God's hand. The powers of this world think they are choosing. God is directing.

Into his right hand comes the divination for Jerusalem, to set battering rams, to open the mouth with murder, to lift up the voice with shouting, to set battering rams against the gates, to cast up mounds, to build siege towers.

The lot falls for Jerusalem. And the verse fills with the sights and sounds of a siege: battering rams, war cries, earth ramps, siege towers.

But to them it will seem like a false divination. They have sworn solemn oaths, but he brings their guilt to remembrance, that they may be taken.

The people of Jerusalem will dismiss it: pagan fortune-telling, it means nothing. They trust their solemn oaths — their treaties and alliances. But behind the pagan omen is God, who brings their guilt to remembrance. They laugh at the method and miss the Master.

verseByVerse.quote: "Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Because you have made your guilt to be remembered, in that your transgressions are uncovered, so that in all your deeds your sins appear—because you have come to remembrance, you shall be taken in hand. And you, O profane wicked one, prince of Israel, whose day has come, the time of your final punishment,
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Because you have made your guilt to be remembered, in that your transgressions are uncovered, so that in all your deeds your sins appear—because you have come to remembrance, you shall be taken in hand.

Four times the idea of remembering and uncovering. Their sins are not forgotten. They are on display in all your deeds. Jerusalem's own behaviour has kept its guilt in God's memory.

Contrast the promise of the new covenant: I will remember their sin no more. The difference is not that some people sin less. It is whether sin is covered by God's atonement or left uncovered to be remembered.

And you, O profane wicked one, prince of Israel, whose day has come, the time of your final punishment,

Now God turns to the king himself: Zedekiah. Profane wicked one. (The ESV notes that wicked one may be read "slain".) He sat on David's throne and swore by God's name, and he profaned both. Whose day has come.

verseByVerse.quote: thus says the Lord GOD: Remove the turban and take off the crown. Things shall not remain as they are. Exalt that which is low, and bring low that which is exalted. A ruin, ruin, ruin I will make it. This also shall not be, until he comes, the one to whom judgment belongs, and I will give it to him.
verseByVerse.commentary:
thus says the Lord GOD: Remove the turban and take off the crown. Things shall not remain as they are. Exalt that which is low, and bring low that which is exalted.

Remove the turban and take off the crown. The ESV uses the same English word, turban, for the high priest's headdress (Exod 28:37). Whatever the exact headdress, the symbols of authority are coming off. Things shall not remain as they are. The old order is ending.

And the principle we heard in 17:24: Exalt that which is low, and bring low that which is exalted. The proud king will be humbled. And, as the next verse shows, one who comes low will be exalted.

A ruin, ruin, ruin I will make it. This also shall not be, until he comes, the one to whom judgment belongs, and I will give it to him.

A ruin, ruin, ruin. Three times, the strongest possible way of saying it. The kingdom, the throne, the crown — ruined.

And then, in the middle of the ruin, a doorway of hope: This also shall not be, until he comes, the one to whom judgment belongs, and I will give it to him. The crown will lie vacant. No king of David's line will wear it — until one comes to whom it rightly belongs.

This echoes Jacob's ancient promise: The scepter shall not depart from Judah... until tribute comes to him; and to him shall be the obedience of the peoples (Gen 49:10). For nearly six centuries after Zedekiah no descendant of David reigned as king in Jerusalem. Then an angel said to a young woman of David's line: the Lord God will give to him the throne of his father David, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever (Luke 1:32-33).

Jesus is the one to whom judgment belongs. The Father... has given all judgment to the Son (John 5:22). He wore a crown of thorns before he wore the crown of glory. And on his robe is written King of kings and Lord of lords (Rev 19:16). The turban and crown were removed from the profane prince so that they could be given to the holy King.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 28–32 — A Sword for the Ammonites
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The Ammonites, who escaped Babylon's choice at the crossroads, are not safe. A sword is drawn for them too, while their diviners see false visions (vv. 28-29). God will judge them in their own land (v. 30), pour out his indignation and hand them to brutal men (v. 31). You shall be no more remembered, for I the LORD have spoken (v. 32).
verseByVerse.theology: Escaping one judgment does not mean escaping God.

verseByVerse.quote: "And you, son of man, prophesy, and say, Thus says the Lord GOD concerning the Ammonites and concerning their reproach; say, A sword, a sword is drawn for the slaughter. It is polished to consume and to flash like lightning— while they see for you false visions, while they divine lies for you—to place you on the necks of the profane wicked, whose day has come, the time of their final punishment. Return it to its sheath. In the place where you were created, in the land of your origin, I will judge you. And I will pour out my indignation upon you; I will blow upon you with the fire of my wrath, and I will deliver you into the hands of brutish men, skillful to destroy. You shall be fuel for the fire. Your blood shall be in the midst of the land. You shall be no more remembered, for I the LORD have spoken."
verseByVerse.commentary:
"And you, son of man, prophesy, and say, Thus says the Lord GOD concerning the Ammonites and concerning their reproach; say, A sword, a sword is drawn for the slaughter. It is polished to consume and to flash like lightning—

The Ammonites might have thought they had escaped. The divination at the crossroads pointed to Jerusalem, not Rabbah. They even mocked Judah's fall (25:3). But the sword song begins again for them: A sword, a sword is drawn.

while they see for you false visions, while they divine lies for you—to place you on the necks of the profane wicked, whose day has come, the time of their final punishment.

Ammon had its own diviners telling it comforting lies. And its fate will be the same as the profane wicked of Judah.

Return it to its sheath. In the place where you were created, in the land of your origin, I will judge you.

And I will pour out my indignation upon you; I will blow upon you with the fire of my wrath, and I will deliver you into the hands of brutish men, skillful to destroy.

You shall be fuel for the fire. Your blood shall be in the midst of the land. You shall be no more remembered, for I the LORD have spoken."

Judah had a future beyond the ruin: until he comes. Ammon is told the opposite: You shall be no more remembered. And Ammon did not endure as a nation.

That is the difference between God's discipline of his people and his judgment on those who remain his enemies. For Judah, judgment was severe but not final; a King was coming. For those outside his covenant mercy, there is no such doorway. Escaping one crisis is not the same as escaping God. The only safe place is under the rule of the King to whom judgment belongs.

21.title: The Sword of the LORD
21.overview:
Ezekiel is to prophesy against Jerusalem: God will draw his sword and cut off both righteous and wicked from the land, and the sword will not return to its sheath. Ezekiel must groan with a breaking heart before the people, and when they ask why, tell them that the news is coming and every heart will melt (vv. 1-7).

He sings of a sword sharpened and polished for slaughter against God's people and their princes, who despised the rod of discipline. He cries out, strikes his thigh and claps his hands as the sword strikes again and again, flashing at every gate, and God himself claps his hands and satisfies his fury (vv. 8-17).

Ezekiel marks a signpost where the road from Babylon forks toward Rabbah of the Ammonites and toward Jerusalem. The king of Babylon stands at the fork and uses divination, and the lot for Jerusalem falls into his right hand. The city thinks it is a false omen, but its guilt is remembered. God tells the profane prince of Israel to remove the turban and crown: things will not stay as they are; the low will be exalted and the exalted brought low. The kingdom will be a ruin, ruin, ruin, until he comes to whom judgment belongs, and God will give it to him (vv. 18-27).

A sword is also drawn against the Ammonites, whose diviners see false visions. God will judge them in their own land, pour out his wrath and hand them to brutal men, and they will be remembered no more (vv. 28-32).
21.theology:
Historical judgments fall on righteous and wicked alike, but they cannot separate believers from the love of Christ (vv. 3-4; 18:20; Matt 5:45; Rom 8:35-37).

The messenger of judgment must feel its weight (vv. 6-7, 12).

Despising God's gentler discipline invites his severer judgment (vv. 10, 13; Prov 3:11-12).

God directs even pagan divination and the decisions of kings (vv. 21-22; Prov 16:33; 21:1).

Sin not covered by God's atonement remains remembered (vv. 23-24).

God removed the crown from David's faithless heir until the coming of the one to whom judgment belongs, Jesus the Son of David (vv. 26-27; Gen 49:10; Luke 1:32-33; John 5:22; Rev 19:16).

Escaping one judgment is not escaping God; for his enemies there is no doorway of hope apart from his King (vv. 28-32).
21.examples:
A sword being polished until it flashes like lightning.

A prophet groaning in public, and people asking why.

A father's rod despised, and a sword coming instead.

The most powerful king on earth reading a sheep's liver at a road junction.

A crown taken off and left waiting.

Ruin, ruin, ruin — until he comes.

22.text: <sup>1</sup>And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,<sup>2</sup>"And you, son of man, will you judge, will you judge the bloody city? Then declare to her all her abominations.<sup>3</sup>You shall say, Thus says the Lord GOD: A city that sheds blood in her midst, so that her time may come, and that makes idols to defile herself!<sup>4</sup>You have become guilty by the blood that you have shed, and defiled by the idols that you have made, and you have brought your days near, the appointed time of your years has come. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations, and a mockery to all the countries.<sup>5</sup>Those who are near and those who are far from you will mock you; your name is defiled; you are full of tumult.<sup>6</sup>"Behold, the princes of Israel in you, every one according to his power, have been bent on shedding blood.<sup>7</sup>Father and mother are treated with contempt in you; the sojourner suffers extortion in your midst; the fatherless and the widow are wronged in you.<sup>8</sup>You have despised my holy things and profaned my Sabbaths.<sup>9</sup>There are men in you who slander to shed blood, and people in you who eat on the mountains; they commit lewdness in your midst.<sup>10</sup>In you men uncover their fathers' nakedness; in you they violate women who are unclean in their menstrual impurity.<sup>11</sup>One commits abomination with his neighbor's wife; another lewdly defiles his daughter-in-law; another in you violates his sister, his father's daughter.<sup>12</sup>In you they take bribes to shed blood; you take interest and profit and make gain of your neighbors by extortion; but me you have forgotten, declares the Lord GOD.<sup>13</sup>"Behold, I strike my hand at the dishonest gain that you have made, and at the blood that has been in your midst.<sup>14</sup>Can your courage endure, or can your hands be strong, in the days that I shall deal with you? I the LORD have spoken, and I will do it.<sup>15</sup>I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you through the countries, and I will consume your uncleanness out of you.<sup>16</sup>And you shall be profaned by your own doing in the sight of the nations, and you shall know that I am the LORD."<sup>17</sup>And the word of the LORD came to me:<sup>18</sup>"Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to me; all of them are bronze and tin and iron and lead in the furnace; they are dross of silver.<sup>19</sup>Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Because you have all become dross, therefore, behold, I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem.<sup>20</sup>As one gathers silver and bronze and iron and lead and tin into a furnace, to blow the fire on it in order to melt it, so I will gather you in my anger and in my wrath, and I will put you in and melt you.<sup>21</sup>I will gather you and blow on you with the fire of my wrath, and you shall be melted in the midst of it.<sup>22</sup>As silver is melted in a furnace, so you shall be melted in the midst of it, and you shall know that I am the LORD; I have poured out my wrath upon you."<sup>23</sup>And the word of the LORD came to me:<sup>24</sup>"Son of man, say to her, You are a land that is not cleansed or rained upon in the day of indignation.<sup>25</sup>The conspiracy of her prophets in her midst is like a roaring lion tearing the prey; they have devoured human lives; they have taken treasure and precious things; they have made many widows in her midst.<sup>26</sup>Her priests have done violence to my law and have profaned my holy things. They have made no distinction between the holy and the common, neither have they taught the difference between the unclean and the clean, and they have disregarded my Sabbaths, so that I am profaned among them.<sup>27</sup>Her princes in her midst are like wolves tearing the prey, shedding blood, destroying lives to get dishonest gain.<sup>28</sup>And her prophets have smeared whitewash for them, seeing false visions and divining lies for them, saying, 'Thus says the Lord GOD,' when the LORD has not spoken.<sup>29</sup>The people of the land have practiced extortion and committed robbery. They have oppressed the poor and needy, and have extorted from the sojourner without justice.<sup>30</sup>And I sought for a man among them who should build up the wall and stand in the breach before me for the land, that I should not destroy it, but I found none.<sup>31</sup>Therefore I have poured out my indignation upon them. I have consumed them with the fire of my wrath. I have returned their way upon their heads, declares the Lord GOD."

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Ezekiel is to confront the bloody city with her abominations (v. 2): bloodshed and idols have brought her day near and made her a mockery (vv. 3-5). Her princes shed blood; parents are despised; sojourners, orphans and widows are oppressed; holy things and Sabbaths are profaned (vv. 6-8). There is slander, idol feasts, sexual corruption, bribery, interest and extortion — but me you have forgotten, declares the Lord GOD (vv. 9-12). God strikes his hand at their dishonest gain; their courage will not endure when he deals with them, and he will scatter them and burn out their uncleanness (vv. 13-16).
verseByVerse.theology: Forgetting God shows itself in every kind of cruelty and corruption toward neighbours.

verseByVerse.quote: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying, "And you, son of man, will you judge, will you judge the bloody city? Then declare to her all her abominations. You shall say, Thus says the Lord GOD: A city that sheds blood in her midst, so that her time may come, and that makes idols to defile herself! You have become guilty by the blood that you have shed, and defiled by the idols that you have made, and you have brought your days near, the appointed time of your years has come. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations, and a mockery to all the countries. Those who are near and those who are far from you will mock you; your name is defiled; you are full of tumult.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

"And you, son of man, will you judge, will you judge the bloody city? Then declare to her all her abominations.

The bloody city. Nahum used the same words of Nineveh, the brutal capital of Assyria: Woe to the bloody city, all full of lies and plunder (Nah 3:1). Now God says them of Jerusalem, the city of his name. Jerusalem has become like the empire that destroyed Samaria.

Ezekiel is made the prosecutor: declare to her all her abominations. What follows reads like a charge sheet.

You shall say, Thus says the Lord GOD: A city that sheds blood in her midst, so that her time may come, and that makes idols to defile herself!

You have become guilty by the blood that you have shed, and defiled by the idols that you have made, and you have brought your days near, the appointed time of your years has come. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations, and a mockery to all the countries.

Two sins sum up the rest: blood and idols. Violence against neighbours and unfaithfulness to God. They always go together. And with them, Jerusalem has brought your days near (the ESV notes that most manuscripts read "until" for part of the line). She is hastening her own end.

Those who are near and those who are far from you will mock you; your name is defiled; you are full of tumult.

Your name is defiled. The city that bore God's name has made that name a joke among the nations.

verseByVerse.quote: "Behold, the princes of Israel in you, every one according to his power, have been bent on shedding blood. Father and mother are treated with contempt in you; the sojourner suffers extortion in your midst; the fatherless and the widow are wronged in you. You have despised my holy things and profaned my Sabbaths.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Behold, the princes of Israel in you, every one according to his power, have been bent on shedding blood.

Every one according to his power. Each leader used as much power as he had to harm others. Power itself is not evil, but in corrupt hands it becomes a weapon. The more power, the more damage.

Father and mother are treated with contempt in you; the sojourner suffers extortion in your midst; the fatherless and the widow are wronged in you.

Now the list moves into the home and the street. Parents are despised — against the command Honor your father and your mother (Exod 20:12). The most vulnerable are exploited: the sojourner (immigrant), the fatherless and the widow. God had told Israel, You shall not wrong a sojourner or oppress him, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt. You shall not mistreat any widow or fatherless child (Exod 22:21-22).

How a society treats its elderly, its foreigners and its fatherless is one of God's measures of its health. James says the same of the church: Religion that is pure and undefiled before God the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction (Jas 1:27).

You have despised my holy things and profaned my Sabbaths.

And toward God: contempt for what is holy. Sin against neighbours and sin against God are never far apart.

verseByVerse.quote: There are men in you who slander to shed blood, and people in you who eat on the mountains; they commit lewdness in your midst. In you men uncover their fathers' nakedness; in you they violate women who are unclean in their menstrual impurity. One commits abomination with his neighbor's wife; another lewdly defiles his daughter-in-law; another in you violates his sister, his father's daughter. In you they take bribes to shed blood; you take interest and profit and make gain of your neighbors by extortion; but me you have forgotten, declares the Lord GOD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
There are men in you who slander to shed blood, and people in you who eat on the mountains; they commit lewdness in your midst.

Men... who slander to shed blood — false accusations that get people killed. The law said, You shall not go around as a slanderer among your people, and you shall not stand up against the life of your neighbor (Lev 19:16). Words can kill.

In you men uncover their fathers' nakedness; in you they violate women who are unclean in their menstrual impurity.

One commits abomination with his neighbor's wife; another lewdly defiles his daughter-in-law; another in you violates his sister, his father's daughter.

The list of sexual sins follows the forbidden relationships of Leviticus 18: incest, adultery, abuse. The family, which God designed as a place of safety, has become a place of violation. These are not private matters. God names them as sins that defile a whole city.

In you they take bribes to shed blood; you take interest and profit and make gain of your neighbors by extortion; but me you have forgotten, declares the Lord GOD.

Bribes that buy death sentences. Interest that exploits the poor (the ESV notes, "profit that comes from charging interest to the poor"). Extortion.

And then the line that explains everything: but me you have forgotten. Every sin on the list flows from this. When God is forgotten, parents are despised, the weak are crushed, bodies are abused and money becomes a god. The root of social collapse is spiritual amnesia.

verseByVerse.quote: "Behold, I strike my hand at the dishonest gain that you have made, and at the blood that has been in your midst. Can your courage endure, or can your hands be strong, in the days that I shall deal with you? I the LORD have spoken, and I will do it. I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you through the countries, and I will consume your uncleanness out of you. And you shall be profaned by your own doing in the sight of the nations, and you shall know that I am the LORD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Behold, I strike my hand at the dishonest gain that you have made, and at the blood that has been in your midst.

God strikes his hand — a gesture of anger and disgust — at the money they made by cheating and the blood they shed. He sees the profit, and he sees the victims.

Can your courage endure, or can your hands be strong, in the days that I shall deal with you? I the LORD have spoken, and I will do it.

Here is a question for everyone who feels strong now. When God deals with you, will your courage last? Who can stand before his indignation? Who can endure the heat of his anger? (Nah 1:6). People who seem bold in sin are not bold before God.

I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you through the countries, and I will consume your uncleanness out of you.

I will consume your uncleanness out of you. The exile will not only punish; it will purify. God's goal is a clean people.

And you shall be profaned by your own doing in the sight of the nations, and you shall know that I am the LORD."

By your own doing. Jerusalem's shame is self-inflicted.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The house of Israel has become dross to me: bronze, tin, iron and lead in the furnace (v. 18). God will gather them into Jerusalem as metal into a furnace and blow on them with the fire of his wrath until they melt (vv. 19-21). As silver is melted in a furnace, so you shall be melted in the midst of it (v. 22).
verseByVerse.theology: God's fire exposes what is worthless; a people who should have been silver are found to be dross.

verseByVerse.quote: And the word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to me; all of them are bronze and tin and iron and lead in the furnace; they are dross of silver. Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Because you have all become dross, therefore, behold, I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem. As one gathers silver and bronze and iron and lead and tin into a furnace, to blow the fire on it in order to melt it, so I will gather you in my anger and in my wrath, and I will put you in and melt you. I will gather you and blow on you with the fire of my wrath, and you shall be melted in the midst of it. As silver is melted in a furnace, so you shall be melted in the midst of it, and you shall know that I am the LORD; I have poured out my wrath upon you."
verseByVerse.commentary:
And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to me; all of them are bronze and tin and iron and lead in the furnace; they are dross of silver.

A new picture from the metalworker's shop. When silver ore is melted in a furnace, the pure silver separates from the worthless impurities — the dross — which is skimmed off and thrown away. Israel was meant to be silver. God says: all of them are dross. Bronze, tin, iron, lead — cheap metals, no silver at all.

Isaiah had said it long before: Your silver has become dross, and I will turn my hand against you and will smelt away your dross (Isa 1:22, 25).

Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Because you have all become dross, therefore, behold, I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem.

As one gathers silver and bronze and iron and lead and tin into a furnace, to blow the fire on it in order to melt it, so I will gather you in my anger and in my wrath, and I will put you in and melt you.

I will gather you and blow on you with the fire of my wrath, and you shall be melted in the midst of it.

As silver is melted in a furnace, so you shall be melted in the midst of it, and you shall know that I am the LORD; I have poured out my wrath upon you."

There is a grim irony here. People from the countryside fled into Jerusalem when the Babylonians came, thinking its walls would protect them — the Rechabites did exactly that (Jer 35:11). God says: I am gathering you into the furnace. The city of refuge becomes the crucible.

For believers, God's fire has a different purpose. The crucible is for silver, and the furnace is for gold, and the LORD tests hearts (Prov 17:3). Christ will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver (Mal 3:3). Trials that come to God's children are refining fire, burning away dross so that what is precious remains. The question every trial asks is: what is left when the fire has done its work?

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 23–31 — I Sought for a Man
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The land is uncleansed (v. 24). Her prophets are like a roaring lion devouring lives (v. 25); her priests do violence to the law and make no distinction between holy and common (v. 26); her princes are like wolves (v. 27); her prophets whitewash it all (v. 28); and the people oppress the poor and the sojourner (v. 29). And I sought for a man among them who should build up the wall and stand in the breach before me for the land, that I should not destroy it, but I found none (v. 30). So God has poured out his indignation (v. 31).
verseByVerse.theology: When every level of a society is corrupt and no intercessor stands in the gap, judgment comes; God himself provided the Man who stands in the breach.

verseByVerse.quote: And the word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, say to her, You are a land that is not cleansed or rained upon in the day of indignation. The conspiracy of her prophets in her midst is like a roaring lion tearing the prey; they have devoured human lives; they have taken treasure and precious things; they have made many widows in her midst. Her priests have done violence to my law and have profaned my holy things. They have made no distinction between the holy and the common, neither have they taught the difference between the unclean and the clean, and they have disregarded my Sabbaths, so that I am profaned among them.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, say to her, You are a land that is not cleansed or rained upon in the day of indignation.

A land with no rain is a land under a curse. No cleansing, no refreshing. Now God walks through the whole society, level by level, to show why.

The conspiracy of her prophets in her midst is like a roaring lion tearing the prey; they have devoured human lives; they have taken treasure and precious things; they have made many widows in her midst.

First, the prophets. Not shepherds but predators — like a roaring lion tearing the prey. It is the same picture Peter uses for the devil: Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour (1 Pet 5:8). False religious leaders do the devil's work. They took money and left widows.

Her priests have done violence to my law and have profaned my holy things. They have made no distinction between the holy and the common, neither have they taught the difference between the unclean and the clean, and they have disregarded my Sabbaths, so that I am profaned among them.

Second, the priests. Their job was to teach the difference: You are to distinguish between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean (Lev 10:10). They blurred every line. When teachers stop teaching the difference between holy and common, right and wrong, the people soon cannot tell.

That is a charge that applies to every pastor and Bible teacher. Our calling is to teach God's distinctions clearly — rightly handling the word of truth (2 Tim 2:15) — not to blur them to make people comfortable.

verseByVerse.quote: Her princes in her midst are like wolves tearing the prey, shedding blood, destroying lives to get dishonest gain. And her prophets have smeared whitewash for them, seeing false visions and divining lies for them, saying, 'Thus says the Lord GOD,' when the LORD has not spoken. The people of the land have practiced extortion and committed robbery. They have oppressed the poor and needy, and have extorted from the sojourner without justice.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Her princes in her midst are like wolves tearing the prey, shedding blood, destroying lives to get dishonest gain.

Third, the princes and officials — like wolves. Zephaniah said the same: Her officials within her are roaring lions; her judges are evening wolves (Zeph 3:3). Jesus warned of ravenous wolves in sheep's clothing (Matt 7:15), and Paul of fierce wolves that would come into the church (Acts 20:29).

And her prophets have smeared whitewash for them, seeing false visions and divining lies for them, saying, 'Thus says the Lord GOD,' when the LORD has not spoken.

And the prophets cover for the princes, smearing whitewash over their crimes (13:10). Religion becomes the public relations department of corruption.

The people of the land have practiced extortion and committed robbery. They have oppressed the poor and needy, and have extorted from the sojourner without justice.

Fourth, the people of the land — the ordinary citizens. They are no better. They too extort, rob and oppress. The rot is not only at the top. From prophets to peasants, the whole society is corrupt. Micah had described the same city: Its heads give judgment for a bribe; its priests teach for a price; its prophets practice divination for money (Mic 3:11).

verseByVerse.quote: And I sought for a man among them who should build up the wall and stand in the breach before me for the land, that I should not destroy it, but I found none. Therefore I have poured out my indignation upon them. I have consumed them with the fire of my wrath. I have returned their way upon their heads, declares the Lord GOD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
And I sought for a man among them who should build up the wall and stand in the breach before me for the land, that I should not destroy it, but I found none.

Here is a heart-searching verse. God himself searches for someone. I sought for a man. One person who would build up the wall and stand in the breach — stand in the gap where the wall is broken, between the people and the judgment, and plead for them.

Moses had done it once. When God was about to destroy Israel after the golden calf, Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach before him, to turn away his wrath (Ps 106:23). Now God looks for another Moses — among the prophets, priests, princes and people. But I found none.

That is a challenge to every believer. Are we willing to stand in the gap for our families, churches and nations in prayer? God still looks for intercessors.

But the deepest answer to this verse is the gospel. Isaiah described the same search: He saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no one to intercede; then his own arm brought him salvation (Isa 59:16). When no human being could stand in the breach, God sent his own Son. There is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus (1 Tim 2:5). He stood in the breach at the cross, taking the judgment on himself. And he always lives to make intercession for those who come to God through him (Heb 7:25). God sought for a man and found none — so he became the Man.

Therefore I have poured out my indignation upon them. I have consumed them with the fire of my wrath. I have returned their way upon their heads, declares the Lord GOD."

With no one in the breach, the wall fell and the judgment came. I have returned their way upon their heads. For Jerusalem, it was too late. For us, the Man in the breach has already come.

22.title: I Sought for a Man
22.overview:
Ezekiel is to confront Jerusalem, the bloody city, with her abominations. Her bloodshed and idols have brought her days to an end and made her a mockery. Her princes use their power to shed blood; parents are despised; sojourners, orphans and widows are oppressed; God's holy things and Sabbaths are profaned. There is slander that leads to murder, idol feasts, incest, adultery and abuse, bribery, exploitative interest and extortion — and God has been forgotten. God strikes his hand at their dishonest gain, asks whether their courage will endure when he deals with them, and promises to scatter them and consume their uncleanness (vv. 1-16).

The house of Israel has become dross — bronze, tin, iron and lead instead of silver. God will gather them into Jerusalem as into a furnace and melt them with the fire of his wrath (vv. 17-22).

The land is uncleansed. Her prophets devour lives like a roaring lion; her priests do violence to the law and do not distinguish holy from common; her princes are like wolves; her prophets whitewash their deeds; and the people oppress the poor and the sojourner. God sought for a man to build up the wall and stand in the breach for the land, but found none. So he has poured out his indignation and returned their way on their heads (vv. 23-31).
22.theology:
Violence against people and idolatry against God belong together; both flow from forgetting God (vv. 3-4, 12).

God measures a society by how it treats parents, foreigners, orphans and widows (v. 7; Exod 22:21-22; Jas 1:27).

No one's courage can endure when God deals with sin (v. 14; Nah 1:6).

God's fire exposes worthless dross in judgment and refines his people in discipline (vv. 18-22; Isa 1:22-25; Prov 17:3; Mal 3:3).

Religious leaders who blur God's distinctions and cover for corruption bear heavy guilt (vv. 25-28; Lev 10:10; Matt 7:15; Acts 20:29).

God looks for intercessors to stand in the breach (v. 30; Ps 106:23).

Where no one could stand in the breach, God sent his Son, the one mediator who intercedes forever (v. 30; Isa 59:16; 1 Tim 2:5; Heb 7:25).
22.examples:
A holy city called by the name of Nineveh.

Leaders using every ounce of their power to harm.

Slander that ends in a death sentence.

A city of refuge turned into a smelting furnace.

Priests who stopped teaching the difference.

A God searching the city for one intercessor.

Finding none, and becoming the Man himself.

23.text: <sup>1</sup>The word of the LORD came to me:<sup>2</sup>"Son of man, there were two women, the daughters of one mother.<sup>3</sup>They played the whore in Egypt; they played the whore in their youth; there their breasts were pressed and their virgin bosoms handled.<sup>4</sup>Oholah was the name of the elder and Oholibah the name of her sister. They became mine, and they bore sons and daughters. As for their names, Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem.<sup>5</sup>"Oholah played the whore while she was mine, and she lusted after her lovers the Assyrians, warriors<sup>6</sup>clothed in purple, governors and commanders, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding on horses.<sup>7</sup>She bestowed her whoring upon them, the choicest men of Assyria all of them, and she defiled herself with all the idols of everyone after whom she lusted.<sup>8</sup>She did not give up her whoring that she had begun in Egypt; for in her youth men had lain with her and handled her virgin bosom and poured out their whoring lust upon her.<sup>9</sup>Therefore I delivered her into the hands of her lovers, into the hands of the Assyrians, after whom she lusted.<sup>10</sup>These uncovered her nakedness; they seized her sons and her daughters; and as for her, they killed her with the sword; and she became a byword among women, when judgment had been executed on her.<sup>11</sup>"Her sister Oholibah saw this, and she became more corrupt than her sister in her lust and in her whoring, which was worse than that of her sister.<sup>12</sup>She lusted after the Assyrians, governors and commanders, warriors clothed in full armor, horsemen riding on horses, all of them desirable young men.<sup>13</sup>And I saw that she was defiled; they both took the same way.<sup>14</sup>But she carried her whoring further. She saw men portrayed on the wall, the images of the Chaldeans portrayed in vermilion,<sup>15</sup>wearing belts on their waists, with flowing turbans on their heads, all of them having the appearance of officers, a likeness of Babylonians whose native land was Chaldea.<sup>16</sup>When she saw them, she lusted after them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.<sup>17</sup>And the Babylonians came to her into the bed of love, and they defiled her with their whoring lust. And after she was defiled by them, she turned from them in disgust.<sup>18</sup>When she carried on her whoring so openly and flaunted her nakedness, I turned in disgust from her, as I had turned in disgust from her sister.<sup>19</sup>Yet she increased her whoring, remembering the days of her youth, when she played the whore in the land of Egypt<sup>20</sup>and lusted after her lovers there, whose members were like those of donkeys, and whose issue was like that of horses.<sup>21</sup>Thus you longed for the lewdness of your youth, when the Egyptians handled your bosom and pressed your young breasts."<sup>22</sup>Therefore, O Oholibah, thus says the Lord GOD: "Behold, I will stir up against you your lovers from whom you turned in disgust, and I will bring them against you from every side:<sup>23</sup>the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, Pekod and Shoa and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them, desirable young men, governors and commanders all of them, officers and men of renown, all of them riding on horses.<sup>24</sup>And they shall come against you from the north with chariots and wagons and a host of peoples. They shall set themselves against you on every side with buckler, shield, and helmet; and I will commit the judgment to them, and they shall judge you according to their judgments.<sup>25</sup>And I will direct my jealousy against you, that they may deal with you in fury. They shall cut off your nose and your ears, and your survivors shall fall by the sword. They shall seize your sons and your daughters, and your survivors shall be devoured by fire.<sup>26</sup>They shall also strip you of your clothes and take away your beautiful jewels.<sup>27</sup>Thus I will put an end to your lewdness and your whoring begun in the land of Egypt, so that you shall not lift up your eyes to them or remember Egypt anymore.<sup>28</sup>"For thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I will deliver you into the hands of those whom you hate, into the hands of those from whom you turned in disgust,<sup>29</sup>and they shall deal with you in hatred and take away all the fruit of your labor and leave you naked and bare, and the nakedness of your whoring shall be uncovered. Your lewdness and your whoring<sup>30</sup>have brought this upon you, because you played the whore with the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.<sup>31</sup>You have gone the way of your sister; therefore I will give her cup into your hand.<sup>32</sup>Thus says the Lord GOD: "You shall drink your sister's cup that is deep and large; you shall be laughed at and held in derision, for it contains much;<sup>33</sup>you will be filled with drunkenness and sorrow. A cup of horror and desolation, the cup of your sister Samaria;<sup>34</sup>you shall drink it and drain it out, and gnaw its shards, and tear your breasts; for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.<sup>35</sup>Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Because you have forgotten me and cast me behind your back, you yourself must bear the consequences of your lewdness and whoring."<sup>36</sup>The LORD said to me: "Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Declare to them their abominations.<sup>37</sup>For they have committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. With their idols they have committed adultery, and they have even offered up to them for food the children whom they had borne to me.<sup>38</sup>Moreover, this they have done to me: they have defiled my sanctuary on the same day and profaned my Sabbaths.<sup>39</sup>For when they had slaughtered their children in sacrifice to their idols, on the same day they came into my sanctuary to profane it. And behold, this is what they did in my house.<sup>40</sup>They even sent for men to come from afar, to whom a messenger was sent; and behold, they came. For them you bathed yourself, painted your eyes, and adorned yourself with ornaments.<sup>41</sup>You sat on a stately couch, with a table spread before it on which you had placed my incense and my oil.<sup>42</sup>The sound of a carefree multitude was with her; and with men of the common sort, drunkards were brought from the wilderness; and they put bracelets on the hands of the women, and beautiful crowns on their heads.<sup>43</sup>"Then I said of her who was worn out by adultery, 'Now they will continue to use her for a whore, even her!'<sup>44</sup>For they have gone in to her, as men go in to a prostitute. Thus they went in to Oholah and to Oholibah, lewd women!<sup>45</sup>But righteous men shall pass judgment on them with the sentence of adulteresses, and with the sentence of women who shed blood, because they are adulteresses, and blood is on their hands."<sup>46</sup>For thus says the Lord GOD: "Bring up a vast host against them, and make them an object of terror and a plunder.<sup>47</sup>And the host shall stone them and cut them down with their swords. They shall kill their sons and their daughters, and burn up their houses.<sup>48</sup>Thus will I put an end to lewdness in the land, that all women may take warning and not commit lewdness as you have done.<sup>49</sup>And they shall return your lewdness upon you, and you shall bear the penalty for your sinful idolatry, and you shall know that I am the Lord GOD."

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Ezekiel tells of two sisters who were unfaithful even in their youth in Egypt (vv. 2-3). Oholah was the name of the elder and Oholibah the name of her sister. They became mine, and they bore sons and daughters. As for their names, Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem (v. 4).
verseByVerse.theology: God's people were unfaithful from the beginning, yet he still made them his own.

verseByVerse.quote: The word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, there were two women, the daughters of one mother. They played the whore in Egypt; they played the whore in their youth; there their breasts were pressed and their virgin bosoms handled. Oholah was the name of the elder and Oholibah the name of her sister. They became mine, and they bore sons and daughters. As for their names, Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, there were two women, the daughters of one mother.

Chapter 23 returns to the picture of chapter 16, but now there are two sisters instead of one. The language is again blunt and disturbing, and deliberately so. God wants his people to be shocked by what their spiritual unfaithfulness looks like.

Verse 3 says both sisters were sexually unfaithful even as girls in Egypt. The point is historical and spiritual: Israel's idolatry did not begin in Canaan. It began in Egypt, before the exodus, as 20:7-8 has already said.

Oholah was the name of the elder and Oholibah the name of her sister. They became mine, and they bore sons and daughters. As for their names, Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem.

The text tells us who they are. Oholah is Samaria, capital of the northern kingdom. Oholibah is Jerusalem, capital of Judah. The two kingdoms came from one people.

And the most striking words are these: They became mine. Despite their unfaithfulness in Egypt, God took them as his own and they bore children to him. Grace came first. Everything that follows is a betrayal of that grace.

Jeremiah had used the same picture of two sisters: Israel was unfaithful and sent away, Yet her treacherous sister Judah did not fear, but she too went and played the whore (Jer 3:8).

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Oholah, while she was God's, lusted after the Assyrians — splendid officers and horsemen — and defiled herself with their idols (vv. 5-7), never giving up the unfaithfulness she began in Egypt (v. 8). So God handed her over to the Assyrians she desired; they stripped her, took her children and killed her, and she became a byword (vv. 9-10).
verseByVerse.theology: The powers we court instead of God become the instruments of our ruin.

verseByVerse.quote: "Oholah played the whore while she was mine, and she lusted after her lovers the Assyrians, warriors clothed in purple, governors and commanders, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding on horses. She bestowed her whoring upon them, the choicest men of Assyria all of them, and she defiled herself with all the idols of everyone after whom she lusted. She did not give up her whoring that she had begun in Egypt; for in her youth men had lain with her and handled her virgin bosom and poured out their whoring lust upon her.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Oholah played the whore while she was mine, and she lusted after her lovers the Assyrians, warriors

clothed in purple, governors and commanders, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding on horses.

Samaria was attracted to Assyria. Notice what attracted her: purple uniforms, officers, cavalry — power and glamour. All of them desirable young men. Assyria was the superpower of the day, and Samaria wanted to be close to it.

This was real history. King Menahem of Israel paid the king of Assyria a thousand talents of silver, that he might help him to confirm his hold on the royal power (2 Kgs 15:19). Political alliance came with religious compromise.

She bestowed her whoring upon them, the choicest men of Assyria all of them, and she defiled herself with all the idols of everyone after whom she lusted.

She defiled herself with all the idols of everyone after whom she lusted. When you give your heart to a power, you take on its gods. Admiring the world's strength and style often ends in adopting its values.

Verse 8 says she never gave up the unfaithfulness she had begun in Egypt. Sin that is not dealt with early does not fade; it grows.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore I delivered her into the hands of her lovers, into the hands of the Assyrians, after whom she lusted. These uncovered her nakedness; they seized her sons and her daughters; and as for her, they killed her with the sword; and she became a byword among women, when judgment had been executed on her.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Therefore I delivered her into the hands of her lovers, into the hands of the Assyrians, after whom she lusted.

Here is the terrible justice of God: I delivered her into the hands of her lovers. The Assyrians she admired became her destroyers. The king of Assyria captured Samaria, and he carried the Israelites away to Assyria (2 Kgs 17:6).

These uncovered her nakedness; they seized her sons and her daughters; and as for her, they killed her with the sword; and she became a byword among women, when judgment had been executed on her.

The things we love in place of God have a way of turning on us. The career that was worshipped consumes the family. The pleasure that was pursued enslaves. The power that was courted crushes. Do not love the world or the things in the world... And the world is passing away along with its desires (1 John 2:15, 17).

She became a byword among women. Samaria's fall became a warning everyone talked about. And that is the point of the next verse: her sister saw it all.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Oholibah saw it all and became worse (v. 11). She too lusted after Assyria (vv. 12-13), and then, seeing the images of the Chaldeans portrayed in vermilion, she sent for the Babylonians (vv. 14-16). When they defiled her she turned from them in disgust, and God turned in disgust from her (vv. 17-18). Yet she went back to the lusts of her youth in Egypt (vv. 19-21).
verseByVerse.theology: A people who have seen God's judgment on others and still follow the same path are more guilty, not less.

verseByVerse.quote: "Her sister Oholibah saw this, and she became more corrupt than her sister in her lust and in her whoring, which was worse than that of her sister. She lusted after the Assyrians, governors and commanders, warriors clothed in full armor, horsemen riding on horses, all of them desirable young men. And I saw that she was defiled; they both took the same way.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Her sister Oholibah saw this, and she became more corrupt than her sister in her lust and in her whoring, which was worse than that of her sister.

Oholibah saw this. Jerusalem watched Samaria fall. She saw exactly where unfaithfulness led. And instead of learning, she became more corrupt than her sister.

That is a dangerous position to be in: to have seen clearly the consequences of sin in someone else's life, and to do it anyway. Knowledge increases responsibility. The child who watched a parent destroyed by addiction, the church that watched another church collapse through compromise — seeing is meant to warn.

She lusted after the Assyrians, governors and commanders, warriors clothed in full armor, horsemen riding on horses, all of them desirable young men.

And I saw that she was defiled; they both took the same way.

Jerusalem too went after Assyria. King Ahaz sent word to the Assyrian king, I am your servant and your son. Come up and rescue me, and paid him with silver and gold found in the house of the LORD (2 Kgs 16:7-8). They both took the same way.

verseByVerse.quote: But she carried her whoring further. She saw men portrayed on the wall, the images of the Chaldeans portrayed in vermilion, wearing belts on their waists, with flowing turbans on their heads, all of them having the appearance of officers, a likeness of Babylonians whose native land was Chaldea. When she saw them, she lusted after them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea. And the Babylonians came to her into the bed of love, and they defiled her with their whoring lust. And after she was defiled by them, she turned from them in disgust. When she carried on her whoring so openly and flaunted her nakedness, I turned in disgust from her, as I had turned in disgust from her sister.
verseByVerse.commentary:
But she carried her whoring further. She saw men portrayed on the wall, the images of the Chaldeans portrayed in vermilion,

wearing belts on their waists, with flowing turbans on their heads, all of them having the appearance of officers, a likeness of Babylonians whose native land was Chaldea.

Now Jerusalem falls in love with pictures. Painted images of Babylonian officers, bright red, in fine belts and turbans. She had not even met them. She was seduced by images.

That is strikingly modern. People are drawn into desires, lifestyles and loyalties through images long before they meet the reality. What we look at shapes what we want. The desires of the eyes are part of what John calls the world (1 John 2:16).

When she saw them, she lusted after them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.

She sent messengers. Judah's flirtation with Babylon went back to Hezekiah, who welcomed Babylonian envoys and showed them everything in his treasure house. Isaiah told him, all that is in your house... shall be carried to Babylon (2 Kgs 20:17).

And the Babylonians came to her into the bed of love, and they defiled her with their whoring lust. And after she was defiled by them, she turned from them in disgust.

When she carried on her whoring so openly and flaunted her nakedness, I turned in disgust from her, as I had turned in disgust from her sister.

Then disillusionment: she turned from them in disgust. Judah became Babylon's vassal and then rebelled. The idol that once dazzled her disgusted her. That is the life cycle of every idol: attraction, indulgence, disgust.

But notice the double disgust. She turned from Babylon; I turned in disgust from her. Her restless unfaithfulness had become repellent to God.

verseByVerse.quote: Yet she increased her whoring, remembering the days of her youth, when she played the whore in the land of Egypt and lusted after her lovers there, whose members were like those of donkeys, and whose issue was like that of horses. Thus you longed for the lewdness of your youth, when the Egyptians handled your bosom and pressed your young breasts."
verseByVerse.commentary:
Yet she increased her whoring, remembering the days of her youth, when she played the whore in the land of Egypt

Having tired of Babylon, Jerusalem went back to her oldest love: Egypt. Verses 20-21 describe it in crude language, meant to disgust. Zedekiah's hope in Egyptian horses and chariots (17:15) was, in God's eyes, not smart politics but a return to the lusts of Israel's youth.

Isaiah had pronounced woe on those who set out to go down to Egypt, without asking for my direction, to take refuge in the protection of Pharaoh (Isa 30:2).

This is how sin works in a life. When one idol fails, the heart does not turn to God. It goes looking for an older idol, one it thought it had outgrown. Remembering the days of her youth — not with repentance, but with longing. Only a new heart breaks that cycle.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: God will stir up the very lovers Oholibah rejected — Babylonians, Chaldeans and Assyrians — against her from every side (vv. 22-24). In his jealousy they will mutilate her, take her children, strip her and end her unfaithfulness (vv. 25-27). She will be given into the hands of those she hates (vv. 28-30). You have gone the way of your sister; therefore I will give her cup into your hand — a cup of horror and desolation she must drain (vv. 31-34). Because you have forgotten me and cast me behind your back, she must bear the consequences (v. 35).
verseByVerse.theology: Those who walk their sister's road must drink their sister's cup — unless another drinks it for them.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore, O Oholibah, thus says the Lord GOD: "Behold, I will stir up against you your lovers from whom you turned in disgust, and I will bring them against you from every side: the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, Pekod and Shoa and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them, desirable young men, governors and commanders all of them, officers and men of renown, all of them riding on horses. And they shall come against you from the north with chariots and wagons and a host of peoples. They shall set themselves against you on every side with buckler, shield, and helmet; and I will commit the judgment to them, and they shall judge you according to their judgments.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Therefore, O Oholibah, thus says the Lord GOD: "Behold, I will stir up against you your lovers from whom you turned in disgust, and I will bring them against you from every side:

The lovers she rejected will come back — as enemies. God himself will stir up them against her.

the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, Pekod and Shoa and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them, desirable young men, governors and commanders all of them, officers and men of renown, all of them riding on horses.

The same glamorous officers and horsemen she admired now ride against her. Pekod, Shoa and Koa were peoples in league with Babylon (Jeremiah names Pekod too, Jer 50:21). The attractive picture on the wall has become a real army at the gate.

And they shall come against you from the north with chariots and wagons and a host of peoples. They shall set themselves against you on every side with buckler, shield, and helmet; and I will commit the judgment to them, and they shall judge you according to their judgments.

They shall judge you according to their judgments. (The ESV notes that the meaning of one Hebrew word in this verse is uncertain.) Jerusalem chose to live by the standards of the nations. Now the nations will judge her by those standards — and they are brutal.

verseByVerse.quote: And I will direct my jealousy against you, that they may deal with you in fury. They shall cut off your nose and your ears, and your survivors shall fall by the sword. They shall seize your sons and your daughters, and your survivors shall be devoured by fire. They shall also strip you of your clothes and take away your beautiful jewels. Thus I will put an end to your lewdness and your whoring begun in the land of Egypt, so that you shall not lift up your eyes to them or remember Egypt anymore.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And I will direct my jealousy against you, that they may deal with you in fury. They shall cut off your nose and your ears, and your survivors shall fall by the sword. They shall seize your sons and your daughters, and your survivors shall be devoured by fire.

I will direct my jealousy against you. Behind Babylon's fury is God's jealousy — the burning love of a husband betrayed. The mutilation of nose and ears was a known punishment in the ancient world. The beauty she used to attract lovers will be destroyed.

They shall also strip you of your clothes and take away your beautiful jewels.

Thus I will put an end to your lewdness and your whoring begun in the land of Egypt, so that you shall not lift up your eyes to them or remember Egypt anymore.

And here is God's purpose in the judgment: I will put an end to your lewdness. The exile would cure Israel of the idolatry that had run from Egypt onward. And in large measure it did. God's severest discipline has a redemptive aim.

verseByVerse.quote: "For thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I will deliver you into the hands of those whom you hate, into the hands of those from whom you turned in disgust, and they shall deal with you in hatred and take away all the fruit of your labor and leave you naked and bare, and the nakedness of your whoring shall be uncovered. Your lewdness and your whoring have brought this upon you, because you played the whore with the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"For thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I will deliver you into the hands of those whom you hate, into the hands of those from whom you turned in disgust,

and they shall deal with you in hatred and take away all the fruit of your labor and leave you naked and bare, and the nakedness of your whoring shall be uncovered. Your lewdness and your whoring

have brought this upon you, because you played the whore with the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.

Those whom you hate. Once she loved them; now she hates them; and she will be handed to them. Everything she worked for — all the fruit of your labor — will be taken.

And the verdict leaves no room for excuses: Your lewdness and your whoring have brought this upon you. Babylon was the instrument, but her own choices were the cause. God does not punish arbitrarily. He gives people over to the harvest of what they sowed.

verseByVerse.quote: You have gone the way of your sister; therefore I will give her cup into your hand. Thus says the Lord GOD: "You shall drink your sister's cup that is deep and large; you shall be laughed at and held in derision, for it contains much; you will be filled with drunkenness and sorrow. A cup of horror and desolation, the cup of your sister Samaria; you shall drink it and drain it out, and gnaw its shards, and tear your breasts; for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD. Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Because you have forgotten me and cast me behind your back, you yourself must bear the consequences of your lewdness and whoring."
verseByVerse.commentary:
You have gone the way of your sister; therefore I will give her cup into your hand.

A new image: a cup. Samaria drank a cup of judgment. Jerusalem walked the same road, so she will drink the same cup.

Thus says the Lord GOD: "You shall drink your sister's cup that is deep and large; you shall be laughed at and held in derision, for it contains much;

you will be filled with drunkenness and sorrow. A cup of horror and desolation, the cup of your sister Samaria;

you shall drink it and drain it out, and gnaw its shards, and tear your breasts; for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.

The cup of God's wrath is a common picture in the prophets. Jeremiah was told, Take from my hand this cup of the wine of wrath (Jer 25:15). Isaiah spoke of Jerusalem having drunk from the hand of the LORD the cup of his wrath (Isa 51:17). Here it is deep and large, full of horror and desolation, drained to the dregs until she gnaws the broken pieces.

And there is one who took that cup into his own hands. In Gethsemane Jesus prayed, Abba, Father, all things are possible for you. Remove this cup from me. Yet not what I will, but what you will (Mark 14:36). He drank the cup of horror and desolation to the bottom, so that God could say to his people, Behold, I have taken from your hand the cup of staggering; the bowl of my wrath you shall drink no more (Isa 51:22).

Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Because you have forgotten me and cast me behind your back, you yourself must bear the consequences of your lewdness and whoring."

Cast me behind your back. The image is vivid: God treated like something tossed over the shoulder and forgotten. God said the same of King Jeroboam (1 Kgs 14:9), and the Levites confessed that Israel cast your law behind their back (Neh 9:26). At the root of all the unfaithfulness is this: you have forgotten me.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Ezekiel is to declare their abominations: adultery with idols and blood on their hands, even offering the children they had borne to God (vv. 36-37). On the very day they sacrificed their children they walked into God's sanctuary (vv. 38-39). They dressed up for envoys from afar and set God's incense and oil on their table (vv. 40-42). Righteous men will judge them as adulteresses and murderers (vv. 43-45). A host will stone them and burn their houses, that all women may take warning, and they will know that he is the Lord GOD (vv. 46-49).
verseByVerse.theology: Worship that goes on alongside idolatry and cruelty is not worship but profanation, and God makes its judgment a warning to all.

verseByVerse.quote: The LORD said to me: "Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Declare to them their abominations. For they have committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. With their idols they have committed adultery, and they have even offered up to them for food the children whom they had borne to me. Moreover, this they have done to me: they have defiled my sanctuary on the same day and profaned my Sabbaths. For when they had slaughtered their children in sacrifice to their idols, on the same day they came into my sanctuary to profane it. And behold, this is what they did in my house.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The LORD said to me: "Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Declare to them their abominations.

For they have committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. With their idols they have committed adultery, and they have even offered up to them for food the children whom they had borne to me.

Two charges: adultery and blood. The adultery is idolatry. The blood includes the most horrifying crime — the children whom they had borne to me, offered to idols (the ESV notes, "made pass through the fire"). Children who belonged to God were given to false gods.

Moreover, this they have done to me: they have defiled my sanctuary on the same day and profaned my Sabbaths.

For when they had slaughtered their children in sacrifice to their idols, on the same day they came into my sanctuary to profane it. And behold, this is what they did in my house.

On the same day. That is the chilling detail. They sacrificed their children to idols, and then — the same day — walked into the LORD's temple for worship, as if nothing had happened.

Jeremiah had seen it: Will you steal, murder, commit adultery... and then come and stand before me in this house... and say, 'We are delivered!' (Jer 7:9-10). It is the ultimate hypocrisy: a religion that makes room for anything, including murder, as long as you turn up to worship. God calls it profaning his sanctuary.

We must ask whether our worship on Sunday is disconnected from how we live on Saturday. God does not accept worship that coexists peacefully with cherished sin.

verseByVerse.quote: They even sent for men to come from afar, to whom a messenger was sent; and behold, they came. For them you bathed yourself, painted your eyes, and adorned yourself with ornaments. You sat on a stately couch, with a table spread before it on which you had placed my incense and my oil. The sound of a carefree multitude was with her; and with men of the common sort, drunkards were brought from the wilderness; and they put bracelets on the hands of the women, and beautiful crowns on their heads.
verseByVerse.commentary:
They even sent for men to come from afar, to whom a messenger was sent; and behold, they came. For them you bathed yourself, painted your eyes, and adorned yourself with ornaments.

Now the picture shows the sisters preparing for foreign guests: bathing, painting their eyes, putting on jewellery. This is diplomacy pictured as seduction — Judah making herself attractive to foreign powers.

You sat on a stately couch, with a table spread before it on which you had placed my incense and my oil.

My incense and my oil. The gifts God gave for his worship were set out on the table to entertain her lovers. The same charge as 16:18. God's gifts used to serve his rivals.

The sound of a carefree multitude was with her; and with men of the common sort, drunkards were brought from the wilderness; and they put bracelets on the hands of the women, and beautiful crowns on their heads.

A carefree party. Drunkards brought in from the desert (the ESV notes, perhaps "Sabeans"). Bracelets and crowns handed out. It is a picture of a people partying with the world while judgment gathers at the gates.

verseByVerse.quote: "Then I said of her who was worn out by adultery, 'Now they will continue to use her for a whore, even her!' For they have gone in to her, as men go in to a prostitute. Thus they went in to Oholah and to Oholibah, lewd women! But righteous men shall pass judgment on them with the sentence of adulteresses, and with the sentence of women who shed blood, because they are adulteresses, and blood is on their hands."
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Then I said of her who was worn out by adultery, 'Now they will continue to use her for a whore, even her!'

For they have gone in to her, as men go in to a prostitute. Thus they went in to Oholah and to Oholibah, lewd women!

Worn out by adultery. The ESV notes that the meaning of verse 43 is uncertain, but the picture is of a woman used up, still being used. That is how the nations treated Israel and Judah — not as valued partners, but as something to exploit and discard.

The world never loves those who sell themselves to it. It uses them. Only God loves faithfully. Friendship with the world is enmity with God (Jas 4:4), and in the end it is also contempt from the world.
