verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Ah, shepherds of Israel who have been feeding yourselves! Should not shepherds feed the sheep? (v. 2). The leaders took the wool and the meat and neglected the flock: the weak not strengthened, the sick not healed, the injured not bandaged, the strayed not brought back, the lost not sought, and all ruled with force and harshness (vv. 3-4). So the sheep scattered and became prey (vv. 5-6). Behold, I am against the shepherds; God will take his sheep out of their mouths (vv. 7-10).
verseByVerse.theology: Those who lead God's people exist to serve the flock, and God holds them to account for how they use it.

verseByVerse.quote: The word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel; prophesy, and say to them, even to the shepherds, Thus says the Lord GOD: Ah, shepherds of Israel who have been feeding yourselves! Should not shepherds feed the sheep? You eat the fat, you clothe yourselves with the wool, you slaughter the fat ones, but you do not feed the sheep.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The word of the LORD came to me:

Now that Jerusalem has fallen and Ezekiel's mouth is opened, the message turns toward hope. And it begins by answering the question: why did the flock end up scattered? Because of its shepherds.

"Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel; prophesy, and say to them, even to the shepherds, Thus says the Lord GOD: Ah, shepherds of Israel who have been feeding yourselves! Should not shepherds feed the sheep?

In the ancient world, kings and leaders were commonly called shepherds. Israel's kings, officials, priests and prophets were meant to be shepherds of God's people. And the charge against them is one simple, devastating question: Should not shepherds feed the sheep?

They had it backwards. Shepherds of Israel who have been feeding yourselves. They treated the flock as something that existed for them.

You eat the fat, you clothe yourselves with the wool, you slaughter the fat ones, but you do not feed the sheep.

Picture a shepherd who shears the sheep for his own coat, eats the best lambs for his dinner, and never leads the flock to pasture. That was Judah's leadership: taxes, privileges, comfort, power — and no care for the people.

This is a searching word for anyone in leadership, and especially for pastors and elders. The temptation to use the flock is always there: for income, for status, for the pleasure of being needed and admired. Peter wrote to elders: shepherd the flock of God that is among you... not for shameful gain, but eagerly; not domineering over those in your charge, but being examples to the flock (1 Pet 5:2-3).

verseByVerse.quote: The weak you have not strengthened, the sick you have not healed, the injured you have not bound up, the strayed you have not brought back, the lost you have not sought, and with force and harshness you have ruled them.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The weak you have not strengthened, the sick you have not healed, the injured you have not bound up, the strayed you have not brought back, the lost you have not sought, and with force and harshness you have ruled them.

Here is a list of five kinds of sheep who needed care, and five failures.

The weak — those without strength to keep up. The sick — those who were ill. The injured — those who had been hurt, who needed their wounds bound up. The strayed — those who had wandered off. The lost — those who were gone altogether and had to be searched for.

Read that list slowly and you have a description of any congregation: the weak in faith, the sick in body and mind, those wounded by life and by other people, the drifting, and the completely lost. A good shepherd notices each kind and goes to each one.

Instead, these shepherds with force and harshness... ruled them. They drove the sheep instead of leading them. They governed by pressure instead of love.

Paul gives the opposite pattern: admonish the idle, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, be patient with them all (1 Thess 5:14). And the pattern for every Christian leader is Christ, who said, I am gentle and lowly in heart (Matt 11:29), and of whom it was said, a bruised reed he will not break (Matt 12:20).

verseByVerse.quote: So they were scattered, because there was no shepherd, and they became food for all the wild beasts. My sheep were scattered; they wandered over all the mountains and on every high hill. My sheep were scattered over all the face of the earth, with none to search or seek for them.
verseByVerse.commentary:
So they were scattered, because there was no shepherd, and they became food for all the wild beasts. My sheep were scattered;

they wandered over all the mountains and on every high hill. My sheep were scattered over all the face of the earth, with none to search or seek for them.

Because there was no shepherd. The shepherds existed, but they did not shepherd. And the result was a scattered flock — wandering on the mountains, falling prey to wild beasts, and nobody looking for them. That was the exile: God's people scattered over all the face of the earth.

Notice God's repeated words: My sheep... My sheep. The flock did not belong to the shepherds. It belonged to God. Whenever leaders forget that the people they lead are God's, not theirs, abuse follows.

Jesus looked at the crowds of his day and saw the same thing: he had compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd (Matt 9:36). And his response was not to condemn the sheep but to care for them: he began to teach them many things (Mark 6:34).

verseByVerse.quote: "Therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD: As I live, declares the Lord GOD, surely because my sheep have become a prey, and my sheep have become food for all the wild beasts, since there was no shepherd, and because my shepherds have not searched for my sheep, but the shepherds have fed themselves, and have not fed my sheep, therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD: Thus says the Lord GOD, Behold, I am against the shepherds, and I will require my sheep at their hand and put a stop to their feeding the sheep. No longer shall the shepherds feed themselves. I will rescue my sheep from their mouths, that they may not be food for them.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD: As I live, declares the Lord GOD, surely because my sheep have become a prey, and my sheep have become food for all the wild beasts, since there was no shepherd, and because my shepherds have not searched for my sheep, but the shepherds have fed themselves, and have not fed my sheep,

God repeats the charge with an oath, as if he cannot let it go. My sheep appears again and again. This is a Shepherd-God who is angry on behalf of his flock.

therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD: Thus says the Lord GOD, Behold, I am against the shepherds, and I will require my sheep at their hand and put a stop to their feeding the sheep. No longer shall the shepherds feed themselves. I will rescue my sheep from their mouths, that they may not be food for them.

Two terrible phrases. I will require my sheep at their hand — every leader will give an account for every soul in his care (Heb 13:17). And I will rescue my sheep from their mouths. The shepherds had become predators. God will pull the sheep out of their teeth.

This is great comfort for anyone who has been hurt by a leader who should have protected them — in a church, a family, a nation. God sees. He is against those shepherds. And he rescues the sheep.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 11–16 — I Myself Will Be the Shepherd
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Behold, I, I myself will search for my sheep and will seek them out (v. 11). God will rescue them from where they were scattered on the dark day, gather them home and feed them on good pasture on the mountains of Israel (vv. 12-14). I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I myself will make them lie down (v. 15). I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak (v. 16).
verseByVerse.theology: Where human shepherds failed, God himself comes to seek, heal and feed his people.

verseByVerse.quote: "For thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I, I myself will search for my sheep and will seek them out. As a shepherd seeks out his flock when he is among his sheep that have been scattered, so will I seek out my sheep, and I will rescue them from all places where they have been scattered on a day of clouds and thick darkness.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"For thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I, I myself will search for my sheep and will seek them out.

Here is the turning point, and a great promise. Behold, I, I myself. God does not say he will find better shepherds first. He says: I will do it myself.

I myself will search for my sheep and will seek them out. The shepherds have not searched (v. 8). God will search. They left the lost unsought. God will seek.

And the New Testament shows how literally God kept this promise. Jesus told of a shepherd who leaves the ninety-nine and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it, and lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing (Luke 15:4-5). And he said of himself: the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost (Luke 19:10). In Jesus, the God of Ezekiel 34 came in person to search for his sheep.

As a shepherd seeks out his flock when he is among his sheep that have been scattered, so will I seek out my sheep, and I will rescue them from all places where they have been scattered on a day of clouds and thick darkness.

A day of clouds and thick darkness was the day of Jerusalem's fall. God knows exactly where each sheep went in the darkness, and he will go there to get it.

If you feel you have wandered far, into a dark place, this is God's word to you: he knows where you are, and he is the kind of shepherd who comes looking.

verseByVerse.quote: And I will bring them out from the peoples and gather them from the countries, and will bring them into their own land. And I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, by the ravines, and in all the inhabited places of the country. I will feed them with good pasture, and on the mountain heights of Israel shall be their grazing land. There they shall lie down in good grazing land, and on rich pasture they shall feed on the mountains of Israel. I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I myself will make them lie down, declares the Lord GOD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And I will bring them out from the peoples and gather them from the countries, and will bring them into their own land. And I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, by the ravines, and in all the inhabited places of the country.

The scattered flock will be gathered — out from the nations, back into their own land. And the same mountains that were cursed for their idolatry (ch. 6) will become pastures.

I will feed them with good pasture, and on the mountain heights of Israel shall be their grazing land. There they shall lie down in good grazing land, and on rich pasture they shall feed on the mountains of Israel.

Good pasture... rich pasture... lie down. The selfish shepherds fed themselves and starved the flock. God feeds the flock. Sheep only lie down when they are full and feel safe.

I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I myself will make them lie down, declares the Lord GOD.

It is impossible to read this without hearing Psalm 23: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul (Ps 23:1-3). Ezekiel 34 is Psalm 23 for a whole scattered nation.

And it is a promise for weary believers now. The Shepherd does not only rescue; he gives rest. Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest (Matt 11:28).

verseByVerse.quote: I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak, and the fat and the strong I will destroy. I will feed them in justice.
verseByVerse.commentary:
I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak, and the fat and the strong I will destroy. I will feed them in justice.

Now compare this verse with verse 4. Point by point, God reverses every failure of the false shepherds.

They did not seek the lost; I will seek the lost. They did not bring back the strayed; I will bring back the strayed. They did not bind up the injured; I will bind up the injured. They did not strengthen the weak; I will strengthen the weak.

That is the heart of God toward his people. He comes for the lost, the drifting, the wounded and the weak. The people the world overlooks are exactly the ones he goes after first.

And the fat and the strong I will destroy. (The ESV notes that the Septuagint, Syriac and Vulgate read "I will watch over".) As the Hebrew stands, the fat and strong are the sheep who, as the next verses show, have grown fat by pushing others aside. I will feed them in justice. God's care for the weak includes justice against those who abuse them.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: God will judge within the flock too, between sheep and sheep (v. 17). Some fat sheep trample the pasture and muddy the water the others must use (vv. 18-19), and push the weak aside with their horns until they scatter (vv. 20-21). I will rescue my flock; they shall no longer be a prey (v. 22).
verseByVerse.theology: God defends the weak members of his flock against the strong who abuse them.

verseByVerse.quote: "As for you, my flock, thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I judge between sheep and sheep, between rams and male goats. Is it not enough for you to feed on the good pasture, that you must tread down with your feet the rest of your pasture; and to drink of clear water, that you must muddy the rest of the water with your feet? And must my sheep eat what you have trodden with your feet, and drink what you have muddied with your feet?
verseByVerse.commentary:
"As for you, my flock, thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I judge between sheep and sheep, between rams and male goats.

Now God turns from the shepherds to the flock itself. Not all the trouble came from the leaders. Among the sheep themselves were some who harmed others. I judge between sheep and sheep.

Jesus used this very picture for the last judgment: he will separate people one from another as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats (Matt 25:32). Belonging to the flock outwardly does not exempt anyone from judgment.

Is it not enough for you to feed on the good pasture, that you must tread down with your feet the rest of your pasture; and to drink of clear water, that you must muddy the rest of the water with your feet?

And must my sheep eat what you have trodden with your feet, and drink what you have muddied with your feet?

Picture strong sheep that eat the best grass and then trample what is left, drink the clear water and then stir up the mud with their hooves. The others get only trampled grass and dirty water.

It is a picture of the powerful within God's own people who take the best for themselves and spoil what is left for others. It happens in churches too: the wealthy honoured and the poor pushed aside. James rebuked exactly this: if you pay attention to the one who wears the fine clothing and say, "You sit here in a good place," while you say to the poor man, "You stand over there"... have you not then made distinctions among yourselves (Jas 2:3-4)?

verseByVerse.quote: "Therefore, thus says the Lord GOD to them: Behold, I, I myself will judge between the fat sheep and the lean sheep. Because you push with side and shoulder, and thrust at all the weak with your horns, till you have scattered them abroad, I will rescue my flock; they shall no longer be a prey. And I will judge between sheep and sheep.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Therefore, thus says the Lord GOD to them: Behold, I, I myself will judge between the fat sheep and the lean sheep.

Again, I, I myself. God takes the side of the lean sheep.

Because you push with side and shoulder, and thrust at all the weak with your horns, till you have scattered them abroad,

The image is physical: pushing with the shoulder, shoving with the side, jabbing with horns, until the weak are driven off. Bullying in the flock.

Believers are called to the opposite: We who are strong have an obligation to bear with the failings of the weak, and not to please ourselves (Rom 15:1). The measure of a healthy church is how it treats its weakest members.

I will rescue my flock; they shall no longer be a prey. And I will judge between sheep and sheep.

I will rescue my flock (the ESV notes, perhaps "save"). The weak will not be left at the mercy of the strong. God himself will step between them.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 23–24 — One Shepherd, My Servant David
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: And I will set up over them one shepherd, my servant David, and he shall feed them: he shall feed them and be their shepherd. And I, the LORD, will be their God, and my servant David shall be prince among them (vv. 23-24).
verseByVerse.theology: The promised Shepherd-King from David's line is Jesus, in whom God himself shepherds his people.

verseByVerse.quote: And I will set up over them one shepherd, my servant David, and he shall feed them: he shall feed them and be their shepherd. And I, the LORD, will be their God, and my servant David shall be prince among them. I am the LORD; I have spoken.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And I will set up over them one shepherd, my servant David, and he shall feed them: he shall feed them and be their shepherd.

Here is the high point of the chapter. God says I myself will be the shepherd (v. 15), and also I will set up over them one shepherd, my servant David. How can both be true?

King David had been dead for four hundred years when Ezekiel wrote this. So my servant David is not David come back to life, but the promised King from David's line — a new David. The prophets spoke of him the same way: David their king, whom I will raise up for them (Jer 30:9). And he will be one shepherd, uniting the scattered and divided people (37:24).

And here the two promises meet in one person. God himself will shepherd his people, and a son of David will shepherd them — because the Son of David is God come in the flesh. Jesus said: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep (John 10:11). He is from David's line (John 7:42), and he is the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls (1 Pet 2:25).

Notice what makes him different from the false shepherds of verse 2. They fed on the sheep. He lays down his life for the sheep. They scattered the flock. He says, there will be one flock, one shepherd (John 10:16). And the prophet Zechariah foresaw the price: Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered — words Jesus applied to himself on the night of his arrest (Matt 26:31). The Good Shepherd was struck so that the flock could be gathered.

And I, the LORD, will be their God, and my servant David shall be prince among them. I am the LORD; I have spoken.

Prince among them — not a distant tyrant, but a ruler who lives among his people. The Word became flesh and dwelt among us (John 1:14). And I am the LORD; I have spoken: this promise is signed and sealed.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: God will make a covenant of peace: wild beasts banished, the flock sleeping safely even in the woods, showers of blessing, fruitful trees and fields, yokes broken (vv. 25-27). They will no more be prey, and none shall make them afraid; no more hunger or reproach (vv. 28-29). They will know that God is with them and they are his people: And you are my sheep, human sheep of my pasture, and I am your God (vv. 30-31).
verseByVerse.theology: The Shepherd's covenant brings security, provision and the joy of belonging to God.

verseByVerse.quote: "I will make with them a covenant of peace and banish wild beasts from the land, so that they may dwell securely in the wilderness and sleep in the woods. And I will make them and the places all around my hill a blessing, and I will send down the showers in their season; they shall be showers of blessing. And the trees of the field shall yield their fruit, and the earth shall yield its increase, and they shall be secure in their land. And they shall know that I am the LORD, when I break the bars of their yoke, and deliver them from the hand of those who enslaved them.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"I will make with them a covenant of peace and banish wild beasts from the land, so that they may dwell securely in the wilderness and sleep in the woods.

A covenant of peace. Peace in the Bible is more than the absence of war. It is wholeness, safety, everything as it should be. God will make a binding agreement to give his people that peace (37:26). And the wild beasts that devoured the scattered sheep (v. 5) will be gone. The flock can sleep safely in the woods — the most dangerous place for sheep.

For Christians, this peace has a name: he himself is our peace, who has made us both one and has broken down in his flesh the dividing wall of hostility (Eph 2:14).

And I will make them and the places all around my hill a blessing, and I will send down the showers in their season; they shall be showers of blessing.

Showers of blessing. Rain at the right time was life in a dry land. The covenant blessings of Leviticus return: I will give you your rains in their season (Lev 26:4). And God's people become a blessing to the places around them, as Abraham was promised.

And the trees of the field shall yield their fruit, and the earth shall yield its increase, and they shall be secure in their land. And they shall know that I am the LORD, when I break the bars of their yoke, and deliver them from the hand of those who enslaved them.

When I break the bars of their yoke. The Shepherd is also a Deliverer, breaking the yoke of slavery. For the exiles it meant freedom from Babylon. For all God's people it points to a deeper freedom: if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed (John 8:36).

verseByVerse.quote: They shall no more be a prey to the nations, nor shall the beasts of the land devour them. They shall dwell securely, and none shall make them afraid. And I will provide for them a renowned place for planting so that they shall no more be consumed with hunger in the land, and no longer suffer the reproach of the nations. And they shall know that I am the LORD their God with them, and that they, the house of Israel, are my people, declares the Lord GOD. And you are my sheep, human sheep of my pasture, and I am your God, declares the Lord GOD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
They shall no more be a prey to the nations, nor shall the beasts of the land devour them. They shall dwell securely, and none shall make them afraid.

None shall make them afraid. Micah pictured the same: they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree, and no one shall make them afraid (Mic 4:4). Fear — of enemies, of hunger, of loss — will be gone.

Jesus says of his sheep: I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand (John 10:28). That is the ultimate security of the flock.

And I will provide for them a renowned place for planting so that they shall no more be consumed with hunger in the land, and no longer suffer the reproach of the nations.

No more hunger; no more shame before the nations. The flock that was mocked will be honoured.

And they shall know that I am the LORD their God with them, and that they, the house of Israel, are my people, declares the Lord GOD.

The LORD their God with them. That is the heart of the covenant: God with his people. The Christmas name of Jesus says exactly this: Immanuel, God with us (Matt 1:23).

And you are my sheep, human sheep of my pasture, and I am your God, declares the Lord GOD."

And the chapter ends by removing the metaphor: human sheep. God is not talking about animals. He is talking about people — you. We are his people, and the sheep of his pasture (Ps 100:3).

The final picture in the Bible is the same: the Lamb in the midst of the throne will be their shepherd, and he will guide them to springs of living water, and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes (Rev 7:17). The Shepherd who was struck becomes the Lamb who shepherds. And the flock he gathers will never be scattered again.

34.title: The Good Shepherd
34.overview:
God condemns the shepherds of Israel, who fed themselves instead of the sheep. They took the wool and the meat but did not strengthen the weak, heal the sick, bind up the injured, bring back the strayed or seek the lost, and they ruled harshly. So the sheep were scattered and devoured. God declares that he is against those shepherds; he will hold them responsible and rescue his sheep from their mouths (vv. 1-10).

God himself will search for his sheep, rescue them from where they were scattered on the day of darkness, gather them home and feed them on good pasture on the mountains of Israel. He himself will be their shepherd and make them lie down. He will seek the lost, bring back the strayed, bind up the injured, strengthen the weak, and feed them in justice (vv. 11-16).

He will also judge between sheep and sheep: the strong who trample the pasture, muddy the water and push the weak away with their horns. He will rescue his flock (vv. 17-22).

God will set over them one shepherd, his servant David, to feed them; the LORD will be their God and David their prince (vv. 23-24).

God will make a covenant of peace with them, banish wild beasts, send showers of blessing, make the land fruitful and break their yoke. They will dwell securely with no one to make them afraid, no longer hungry or shamed. They will know that the LORD their God is with them and that they are his people — his human sheep, and he their God (vv. 25-31).
34.theology:
Leaders of God's people are shepherds who exist to serve the flock, and God will require his sheep at their hand (vv. 2-10; 1 Pet 5:2-3; Acts 20:28; Heb 13:17).

Faithful shepherding cares for the weak, sick, injured, straying and lost, and rules with gentleness, not force (vv. 4, 16; 1 Thess 5:14; Matt 12:20).

Where human shepherds fail, God himself comes to seek and save his people (vv. 11-16; Ps 23:1-3; Luke 15:4-7; 19:10).

God judges within the flock and defends the weak against the strong (vv. 17-22; Matt 25:31-33; Jas 2:1-6; Rom 15:1).

The promised Shepherd, God's servant David, is Jesus, God in the flesh from David's line, who lays down his life for the sheep and gathers one flock (vv. 23-24; Jer 30:9; John 10:11-16; Matt 26:31).

The Shepherd's covenant of peace brings security, provision, freedom and the presence of God (vv. 25-31; Eph 2:14; John 10:28; Rev 7:17).
34.examples:
A shepherd wearing a coat made from his flock's wool, while the sheep go hungry.

Five sheep: weak, sick, injured, straying, lost.

Behold, I, I myself will search.

A shepherd carrying a lost sheep home on his shoulders.

Strong sheep muddying the water after they drink.

A shepherd who lays down his life.

Sheep sleeping safely in the woods.

You are my sheep, human sheep of my pasture.

35.text: <sup>1</sup>The word of the LORD came to me:<sup>2</sup>"Son of man, set your face against Mount Seir, and prophesy against it,<sup>3</sup>and say to it, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am against you, Mount Seir, and I will stretch out my hand against you, and I will make you a desolation and a waste.<sup>4</sup>I will lay your cities waste, and you shall become a desolation, and you shall know that I am the LORD.<sup>5</sup>Because you cherished perpetual enmity and gave over the people of Israel to the power of the sword at the time of their calamity, at the time of their final punishment,<sup>6</sup>therefore, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will prepare you for blood, and blood shall pursue you; because you did not hate bloodshed, therefore blood shall pursue you.<sup>7</sup>I will make Mount Seir a waste and a desolation, and I will cut off from it all who come and go.<sup>8</sup>And I will fill its mountains with the slain. On your hills and in your valleys and in all your ravines those slain with the sword shall fall.<sup>9</sup>I will make you a perpetual desolation, and your cities shall not be inhabited. Then you will know that I am the LORD.<sup>10</sup>"Because you said, 'These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will take possession of them'—although the LORD was there—<sup>11</sup>therefore, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will deal with you according to the anger and envy that you showed because of your hatred against them. And I will make myself known among them, when I judge you.<sup>12</sup>And you shall know that I am the LORD. "I have heard all the revilings that you uttered against the mountains of Israel, saying, 'They are laid desolate; they are given us to devour.'<sup>13</sup>And you magnified yourselves against me with your mouth, and multiplied your words against me; I heard it.<sup>14</sup>Thus says the Lord GOD: While the whole earth rejoices, I will make you desolate.<sup>15</sup>As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate, so I will deal with you; you shall be desolate, Mount Seir, and all Edom, all of it. Then they will know that I am the LORD.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: God sets his face against Mount Seir, Edom's mountain homeland, to make it a desolation (vv. 1-4), Because you cherished perpetual enmity and gave over the people of Israel to the power of the sword at the time of their calamity (v. 5). Because you did not hate bloodshed, therefore blood shall pursue you (v. 6). Its hills will be filled with the slain and it will be a perpetual desolation (vv. 7-9).
verseByVerse.theology: Hatred nursed for generations reaps what it sows.

verseByVerse.quote: The word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, set your face against Mount Seir, and prophesy against it, and say to it, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am against you, Mount Seir, and I will stretch out my hand against you, and I will make you a desolation and a waste. I will lay your cities waste, and you shall become a desolation, and you shall know that I am the LORD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, set your face against Mount Seir, and prophesy against it,

Why another oracle against Edom, when chapter 25 has already judged it? Because of where this one is placed. Chapter 35 speaks to Mount Seir, Edom's mountains; chapter 36 speaks to the mountains of Israel. The two chapters belong together. Edom's mountains will be made desolate; Israel's mountains will be made fruitful again. The enemy who wanted Israel's land will lose its own.

and say to it, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am against you, Mount Seir, and I will stretch out my hand against you, and I will make you a desolation and a waste. I will lay your cities waste, and you shall become a desolation, and you shall know that I am the LORD.

A desolation and a waste. The word desolation comes again and again in this chapter. Edom rejoiced when Israel was desolate. It will learn what desolation is.

verseByVerse.quote: Because you cherished perpetual enmity and gave over the people of Israel to the power of the sword at the time of their calamity, at the time of their final punishment, therefore, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will prepare you for blood, and blood shall pursue you; because you did not hate bloodshed, therefore blood shall pursue you. I will make Mount Seir a waste and a desolation, and I will cut off from it all who come and go. And I will fill its mountains with the slain. On your hills and in your valleys and in all your ravines those slain with the sword shall fall. I will make you a perpetual desolation, and your cities shall not be inhabited. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Because you cherished perpetual enmity and gave over the people of Israel to the power of the sword at the time of their calamity, at the time of their final punishment,

You cherished perpetual enmity. Edom's hatred of Israel went back to the brothers Esau and Jacob. Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing, and said, I will kill my brother Jacob (Gen 27:41). Centuries later Amos said Edom pursued his brother with the sword and cast off all pity, and his anger tore perpetually (Amos 1:11).

And notice the word cherished. Edom did not just feel hatred. It nursed it, kept it alive, handed it down. And when Israel was at its lowest — at the time of their calamity — Edom joined in, handing fugitives over to the sword.

A grudge cherished long enough becomes cruelty. That is true of nations, families and individuals. What we refuse to forgive, we eventually act on.

therefore, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will prepare you for blood, and blood shall pursue you; because you did not hate bloodshed, therefore blood shall pursue you.

You did not hate bloodshed. Edom was comfortable with violence. So blood shall pursue you. Jesus stated the principle simply: all who take the sword will perish by the sword (Matt 26:52). Whatever one sows, that will he also reap (Gal 6:7).

I will make Mount Seir a waste and a desolation, and I will cut off from it all who come and go. And I will fill its mountains with the slain... I will make you a perpetual desolation, and your cities shall not be inhabited. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

Perpetual enmity leads to perpetual desolation. The punishment matches the sin.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 10–15 — Although the LORD Was There
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Edom planned to take both Israel and Judah — although the LORD was there (v. 10). God will repay its anger and envy (v. 11). He heard every insult against the mountains of Israel, and every boast was really against him: I heard it (vv. 12-13). As Edom rejoiced over Israel's desolation, so Edom will be desolate (vv. 14-15).
verseByVerse.theology: Those who attack God's people attack God, and he hears every word.

verseByVerse.quote: "Because you said, 'These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will take possession of them'—although the LORD was there— therefore, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will deal with you according to the anger and envy that you showed because of your hatred against them. And I will make myself known among them, when I judge you. And you shall know that I am the LORD. "I have heard all the revilings that you uttered against the mountains of Israel, saying, 'They are laid desolate; they are given us to devour.' And you magnified yourselves against me with your mouth, and multiplied your words against me; I heard it.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Because you said, 'These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will take possession of them'—although the LORD was there—

Edom's ambition: with Israel and Judah both destroyed, their land was up for grabs. These two nations and these two countries shall be mine.

And then God's quiet, devastating phrase: although the LORD was there. Edom looked at the empty land and saw vacant property. God says: I was there. The land was desolate, the temple burned, the people gone — but the LORD had not left his land. It was still his.

This is a great comfort for God's people in times of loss. A church may be small, a believer may be broken, a situation may look abandoned — but the LORD was there. What looks empty to the enemy is still under the ownership of God.

therefore, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will deal with you according to the anger and envy that you showed because of your hatred against them. And I will make myself known among them, when I judge you.

Anger and envy. Envy was at the root of Esau's hatred from the start — envy of his brother's blessing. And God will deal with Edom according to it.

And you shall know that I am the LORD. "I have heard all the revilings that you uttered against the mountains of Israel, saying, 'They are laid desolate; they are given us to devour.'

And you magnified yourselves against me with your mouth, and multiplied your words against me; I heard it.

Edom insulted Israel's mountains, and God says: you magnified yourselves against me. To mock God's people is to mock God. When Saul persecuted the church, the risen Jesus asked, why are you persecuting me? (Acts 9:4).

And three short words: I heard it. Every word spoken against God's people is heard. On the day of judgment people will give account for every careless word they speak (Matt 12:36).

verseByVerse.quote: Thus says the Lord GOD: While the whole earth rejoices, I will make you desolate. As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate, so I will deal with you; you shall be desolate, Mount Seir, and all Edom, all of it. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Thus says the Lord GOD: While the whole earth rejoices, I will make you desolate.

As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate, so I will deal with you; you shall be desolate, Mount Seir, and all Edom, all of it. Then they will know that I am the LORD.

The judgment mirrors the sin exactly. Edom rejoiced at Israel's desolation; the whole earth will rejoice at Edom's. As you have done, it shall be done to you (Obad 15).

The story of Esau and Jacob runs all the way into the New Testament. Esau is remembered as the one who sold his birthright for a single meal and later found no chance to repent, though he sought it with tears (Heb 12:16-17). And when the true Son of Jacob was born in Bethlehem, the king who tried to kill him was Herod — an Idumean, of Edomite descent (Matt 2:16). The ancient enmity reached out against the Messiah himself.

But God's King was not destroyed by Edom's hatred. And the gospel that went out from him reaches every people, calling even the heirs of old enmities to lay down their hatred and be reconciled to God and to one another.

35.title: Against Mount Seir
35.overview:
God sets his face against Mount Seir, the homeland of Edom, and will make it a desolation, because Edom cherished perpetual enmity against Israel and handed Israel over to the sword in their time of calamity. Because Edom did not hate bloodshed, blood will pursue it; its mountains will be filled with the slain and it will be a perpetual desolation (vv. 1-9).

Edom planned to seize both Israel and Judah, though the LORD was there. God will repay its anger and envy. He heard every insult Edom spoke against the mountains of Israel, and every boast against him. As Edom rejoiced over Israel's desolation, so all Edom will be desolate, and they will know that he is the LORD (vv. 10-15).
35.theology:
Hatred cherished over generations becomes cruelty and reaps judgment (vv. 5-6; Gen 27:41; Amos 1:11; Matt 26:52; Gal 6:7).

God has not abandoned what is his, even when it lies desolate (v. 10).

To attack or mock God's people is to attack God; he hears every word (vv. 12-13; Acts 9:4; Matt 12:36-37).

God's judgment often mirrors the sin it punishes (vv. 6, 15; Obad 15).
35.examples:
A grudge kept alive for centuries.

A nation comfortable with bloodshed.

Vacant property — although the LORD was there.

Three words: I heard it.

Rejoicing at a brother's ruin, and being rejoiced over.

The cities shall be inhabited and the waste places rebuilt.<sup>11</sup>And I will multiply on you man and beast, and they shall multiply and be fruitful. And I will cause you to be inhabited as in your former times, and will do more good to you than ever before. Then you will know that I am the LORD.<sup>12</sup>I will let people walk on you, even my people Israel. And they shall possess you, and you shall be their inheritance, and you shall no longer bereave them of children.<sup>13</sup>Thus says the Lord GOD: Because they say to you, 'You devour people, and you bereave your nation of children,'<sup>14</sup>therefore you shall no longer devour people and no longer bereave your nation of children, declares the Lord GOD.<sup>15</sup>And I will not let you hear anymore the reproach of the nations, and you shall no longer bear the disgrace of the peoples and no longer cause your nation to stumble, declares the Lord GOD."<sup>16</sup>The word of the LORD came to me:<sup>17</sup>"Son of man, when the house of Israel lived in their own land, they defiled it by their ways and their deeds. Their ways before me were like the uncleanness of a woman in her menstrual impurity.<sup>18</sup>So I poured out my wrath upon them for the blood that they had shed in the land, for the idols with which they had defiled it.<sup>19</sup>I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed through the countries. In accordance with their ways and their deeds I judged them.<sup>20</sup>But when they came to the nations, wherever they came, they profaned my holy name, in that people said of them, 'These are the people of the LORD, and yet they had to go out of his land.'<sup>21</sup>But I had concern for my holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations to which they came.<sup>22</sup>"Therefore say to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord GOD: It is not for your sake, O house of Israel, that I am about to act, but for the sake of my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations to which you came.<sup>23</sup>And I will vindicate the holiness of my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, and which you have profaned among them. And the nations will know that I am the LORD, declares the Lord GOD, when through you I vindicate my holiness before their eyes.<sup>24</sup>I will take you from the nations and gather you from all the countries and bring you into your own land.<sup>25</sup>I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.<sup>26</sup>And I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you. And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.<sup>27</sup>And I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes and be careful to obey my rules.<sup>28</sup>You shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers, and you shall be my people, and I will be your God.<sup>29</sup>And I will deliver you from all your uncleannesses. And I will summon the grain and make it abundant and lay no famine upon you.<sup>30</sup>I will make the fruit of the tree and the increase of the field abundant, that you may never again suffer the disgrace of famine among the nations.<sup>31</sup>Then you will remember your evil ways, and your deeds that were not good, and you will loathe yourselves for your iniquities and your abominations.<sup>32</sup>It is not for your sake that I will act, declares the Lord GOD; let that be known to you. I am the LORD; I have spoken, and I will do it.<sup>37</sup>"Thus says the Lord GOD: This also I will let the house of Israel ask me to do for them: to increase their people like a flock.<sup>38</sup>Like the flock for sacrifices, like the flock at Jerusalem during her appointed feasts, so shall the waste cities be filled with flocks of people. Then they will know that I am the LORD."

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Ezekiel speaks to the mountains of Israel (v. 1). Enemies said Aha! and claimed the ancient heights; the land was crushed, plundered and mocked (vv. 2-4). In hot jealousy God has spoken against the nations and Edom, who seized his land with joy and contempt (vv. 5-6), and I swear that the nations that are all around you shall themselves suffer reproach (v. 7).
verseByVerse.theology: God is jealous for his land and his people, and the mockers will be mocked.

verseByVerse.quote: "And you, son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel, and say, O mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD. Thus says the Lord GOD: Because the enemy said of you, 'Aha!' and, 'The ancient heights have become our possession,' therefore prophesy, and say, Thus says the Lord GOD: Precisely because they made you desolate and crushed you from all sides, so that you became the possession of the rest of the nations, and you became the talk and evil gossip of the people, therefore, O mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD: Thus says the Lord GOD to the mountains and the hills, the ravines and the valleys, the desolate wastes and the deserted cities, which have become a prey and derision to the rest of the nations all around, therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Surely I have spoken in my hot jealousy against the rest of the nations and against all Edom, who gave my land to themselves as a possession with wholehearted joy and utter contempt, that they might make its pasturelands a prey.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"And you, son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel, and say, O mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD.

In chapter 6 Ezekiel prophesied against the mountains of Israel, where the idol shrines stood. In chapter 35 he prophesied against Mount Seir. Now he turns to the mountains of Israel again — and this time the message is hope.

Thus says the Lord GOD: Because the enemy said of you, 'Aha!' and, 'The ancient heights have become our possession,'

therefore prophesy, and say, Thus says the Lord GOD: Precisely because they made you desolate and crushed you from all sides, so that you became the possession of the rest of the nations, and you became the talk and evil gossip of the people,

The land itself is pictured as a victim: crushed, seized, and gossiped about. The talk and evil gossip of the people. The world talked about Israel's ruin with contempt.

therefore, O mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD: Thus says the Lord GOD to the mountains and the hills, the ravines and the valleys, the desolate wastes and the deserted cities, which have become a prey and derision to the rest of the nations all around,

God addresses every part of the landscape: mountains, hills, ravines, valleys, ruins, empty cities. Not one corner is forgotten.

therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Surely I have spoken in my hot jealousy against the rest of the nations and against all Edom, who gave my land to themselves as a possession with wholehearted joy and utter contempt, that they might make its pasturelands a prey.

My land. The nations thought they were taking empty territory. God calls it his. And he speaks in my hot jealousy — the jealousy of an owner and a husband who will not let what is his be treated with utter contempt.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel, and say to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I have spoken in my jealous wrath, because you have suffered the reproach of the nations. Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: I swear that the nations that are all around you shall themselves suffer reproach.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel, and say to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I have spoken in my jealous wrath, because you have suffered the reproach of the nations.

Because you have suffered the reproach of the nations. God takes the side of his humiliated people. He was the one who judged them, but he will not let their enemies have the last laugh.

Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: I swear that the nations that are all around you shall themselves suffer reproach.

I swear. God binds himself by oath on behalf of his people. The mockers will be mocked.

For believers who have been ridiculed for their faith, or who have watched the church become the object of contempt, this is steadying. God's discipline of his people does not mean he has handed them to their enemies forever.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: But you, O mountains of Israel, shall shoot forth your branches and yield your fruit to my people Israel, for they will soon come home. For behold, I am for you (vv. 8-9). The land will be tilled and sown, filled with people and animals, its cities rebuilt, and God will do more good to you than ever before (vv. 10-11). The land that once devoured its people will no longer bereave them of children or bear the reproach of the nations (vv. 12-15).
verseByVerse.theology: The God who was against his sinful people declares himself for them, and does more good than before.

verseByVerse.quote: "But you, O mountains of Israel, shall shoot forth your branches and yield your fruit to my people Israel, for they will soon come home. For behold, I am for you, and I will turn to you, and you shall be tilled and sown. And I will multiply people on you, the whole house of Israel, all of it. The cities shall be inhabited and the waste places rebuilt. And I will multiply on you man and beast, and they shall multiply and be fruitful. And I will cause you to be inhabited as in your former times, and will do more good to you than ever before. Then you will know that I am the LORD. I will let people walk on you, even my people Israel. And they shall possess you, and you shall be their inheritance, and you shall no longer bereave them of children.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"But you, O mountains of Israel, shall shoot forth your branches and yield your fruit to my people Israel, for they will soon come home.

But you. After all the desolation, God speaks to the land as if it were a garden waiting for its people. The trees will put out branches and fruit — for Israel, for they will soon come home. The land is told to get ready.

For behold, I am for you, and I will turn to you, and you shall be tilled and sown.

Here are four beautiful words: I am for you. Throughout the book God has said, I am against you (5:8; 13:8; 21:3; 26:3; 29:3). Now: I am for you. Paul draws the same conclusion for everyone in Christ: If God is for us, who can be against us? (Rom 8:31).

And I will multiply people on you, the whole house of Israel, all of it. The cities shall be inhabited and the waste places rebuilt.

The whole house of Israel, all of it. Not only Judah, but the northern tribes lost long before. The divided people will be one again, as the next chapter will show: they shall be no longer two nations, and no longer divided into two kingdoms (37:22). God's restoration reaches further back than anyone dared hope.

And I will multiply on you man and beast, and they shall multiply and be fruitful. And I will cause you to be inhabited as in your former times, and will do more good to you than ever before. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

And will do more good to you than ever before. God's restoration is not merely putting things back as they were. It is better than before. That is how God works: after the cross comes not just a return to life but resurrection life; after the fall of Eden comes not Eden restored but the new creation.

I will let people walk on you, even my people Israel. And they shall possess you, and you shall be their inheritance, and you shall no longer bereave them of children.

You shall be their inheritance. The land is given back as a family inheritance, a gift passed from God to his children. The New Testament widens the horizon: Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth (Matt 5:5). The promise to Israel's mountains is a foretaste of a whole renewed earth given to God's people.

verseByVerse.quote: Thus says the Lord GOD: Because they say to you, 'You devour people, and you bereave your nation of children,' therefore you shall no longer devour people and no longer bereave your nation of children, declares the Lord GOD. And I will not let you hear anymore the reproach of the nations, and you shall no longer bear the disgrace of the peoples and no longer cause your nation to stumble, declares the Lord GOD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
Thus says the Lord GOD: Because they say to you, 'You devour people, and you bereave your nation of children,'

The nations said the land of Israel was cursed — You devour people. It was the same slander the spies spread in the wilderness, calling Canaan a land that devours its inhabitants (Num 13:32). Famine, war and exile had made it seem true.

therefore you shall no longer devour people and no longer bereave your nation of children, declares the Lord GOD.

And I will not let you hear anymore the reproach of the nations, and you shall no longer bear the disgrace of the peoples and no longer cause your nation to stumble, declares the Lord GOD."

The land will stop being a place of death and shame. No more lost children, no more mockery, no more stumbling. When God restores, he removes not only the suffering but the shame that went with it.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 16–23 — For the Sake of My Holy Name
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Israel defiled the land with blood and idols, so God scattered them (vv. 16-19). But wherever they went they profaned his holy name, because people said, These are the people of the LORD, and yet they had to go out of his land (vv. 20-21). It is not for your sake, O house of Israel, that I am about to act, but for the sake of my holy name (v. 22), and he will vindicate the holiness of his great name before the nations (v. 23).
verseByVerse.theology: God saves his people not because they deserve it but to vindicate the holiness of his own name.

verseByVerse.quote: The word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, when the house of Israel lived in their own land, they defiled it by their ways and their deeds. Their ways before me were like the uncleanness of a woman in her menstrual impurity. So I poured out my wrath upon them for the blood that they had shed in the land, for the idols with which they had defiled it. I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed through the countries. In accordance with their ways and their deeds I judged them.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, when the house of Israel lived in their own land, they defiled it by their ways and their deeds. Their ways before me were like the uncleanness of a woman in her menstrual impurity.

Now God explains why he will restore them — and the explanation begins with a blunt reminder of why they were scattered. They defiled the land. The picture of ritual impurity shows how God saw their lives: unclean, making the land unfit for his presence.

So I poured out my wrath upon them for the blood that they had shed in the land, for the idols with which they had defiled it. I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed through the countries. In accordance with their ways and their deeds I judged them.

Blood and idols — violence and false worship, the two charges that run through the whole book. The exile was just: In accordance with their ways and their deeds I judged them. God does not pretend they deserved restoration.

verseByVerse.quote: But when they came to the nations, wherever they came, they profaned my holy name, in that people said of them, 'These are the people of the LORD, and yet they had to go out of his land.' But I had concern for my holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations to which they came.
verseByVerse.commentary:
But when they came to the nations, wherever they came, they profaned my holy name, in that people said of them, 'These are the people of the LORD, and yet they had to go out of his land.'

Here is a problem. Scattering Israel among the nations brought a new dishonour on God. People looked at the refugees and said, These are the people of the LORD, and yet they had to go out of his land. In other words: what kind of God cannot keep his own people in his own land? Either he is weak, or he does not care.

That is still how the world often judges God — by the condition of his people. When the church is weak, divided or disgraced, people conclude that its God is not real or not powerful. Paul quoted the same charge: The name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you (Rom 2:24).

But I had concern for my holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations to which they came.

I had concern for my holy name. God cares about his reputation — not out of vanity, but because his name is his true character, and the world's salvation depends on knowing it truly.

This is exactly what Jesus taught us to pray first: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name (Matt 6:9). Before our needs, before our requests, we ask God to do what Ezekiel 36 promises — to make his name known as holy in the world. And we pray it knowing that our own lives have often done the opposite.

verseByVerse.quote: "Therefore say to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord GOD: It is not for your sake, O house of Israel, that I am about to act, but for the sake of my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations to which you came. And I will vindicate the holiness of my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, and which you have profaned among them. And the nations will know that I am the LORD, declares the Lord GOD, when through you I vindicate my holiness before their eyes.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Therefore say to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord GOD: It is not for your sake, O house of Israel, that I am about to act, but for the sake of my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations to which you came.

Read this slowly, because it is the foundation of everything that follows: It is not for your sake... that I am about to act, but for the sake of my holy name.

At first this may sound cold. It is actually the most secure ground of salvation there could be. If God saved Israel because Israel deserved it, the promise would be worthless, because Israel did not deserve it. If God saves for the sake of his own name, the promise is as certain as God himself. Moses had told Israel the same long before: Not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart (Deut 9:5).

This is grace. It humbles us and it steadies us. Not to us, O LORD, not to us, but to your name give glory (Ps 115:1). For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing (Eph 2:8).

And I will vindicate the holiness of my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, and which you have profaned among them. And the nations will know that I am the LORD, declares the Lord GOD, when through you I vindicate my holiness before their eyes.

Through you I vindicate my holiness before their eyes. The very people who dishonoured God's name will become the proof of his holiness. How? Not by trying harder, but by being transformed by God. A changed people is God's answer to the world's contempt.

Peter gives the same calling to Christians scattered among the nations: Keep your conduct among the Gentiles honorable, so that when they speak against you as evildoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God (1 Pet 2:12). A people changed by God's Spirit is the best answer to a world that doubts God.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 24–32 — A New Heart and a New Spirit
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: God will gather them home (v. 24). I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses... And I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you. And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh. And I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes (vv. 25-27). They will be his people in a fruitful land (vv. 28-30), and they will remember their ways and loathe themselves, knowing it was not for their sake (vv. 31-32).
verseByVerse.theology: God promises to cleanse his people, replace their hearts and put his own Spirit within them, so that they obey him from within.

verseByVerse.quote: I will take you from the nations and gather you from all the countries and bring you into your own land. I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
verseByVerse.commentary:
I will take you from the nations and gather you from all the countries and bring you into your own land.

First, a new exodus: gathered from every nation and brought home.

And the gathering does not stop at Israel's borders. John tells us that Jesus would die not for the nation only, but also to gather into one the children of God who are scattered abroad (John 11:52). The ingathering Ezekiel foresaw widened, through Christ, to people from every nation.

I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.

Second, cleansing. The people were unclean (v. 17). God does not tell them to wash themselves. I will sprinkle clean water on you. It is the language of the priest's purification rites, where water was sprinkled to make the unclean clean. From all your uncleannesses... from all your idols. Nothing is left out.

The New Testament speaks of this cleansing in Christ: you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God (1 Cor 6:11). We draw near to God with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water (Heb 10:22).

If you feel stained by your past, this is God's promise. He does not ask you to scrub yourself clean before you come. He does the cleansing.

And notice: from all your idols I will cleanse you. God's cleansing reaches the idols of the heart (14:3), not only the stains of conduct. The Thessalonians were a picture of it: they turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God (1 Thess 1:9).

verseByVerse.quote: And I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you. And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you. And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.

Here is the centre of the chapter, and a promise at the heart of the Old Testament's hope.

Israel's problem was never merely that they lacked good laws or good leaders. It was their hearts. A heart of stone — cold, hard, unresponsive to God no matter how many prophets he sent. Ezekiel had said it again and again. And no amount of reform could fix a heart of stone. You cannot soften a stone by lecturing it.

So God promises something only he can do. Not repair, but replacement. I will remove the heart of stone... and give you a heart of flesh. A living heart, responsive, able to love, grieve, repent and rejoice. A new heart, and a new spirit — a new inner life.

Earlier God commanded, make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit! (18:31). Now he promises to give it. What he requires, he provides. That is the gospel in the Old Testament.

Moses had foreseen it: the LORD your God will circumcise your heart... so that you will love the LORD your God with all your heart (Deut 30:6). David prayed for it: Create in me a clean heart, O God (Ps 51:10). And Jesus called it being born again.

verseByVerse.quote: And I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes and be careful to obey my rules.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes and be careful to obey my rules.

And then the greatest gift: I will put my Spirit within you. Not only a new spirit, but my Spirit — God himself living inside his people.

And notice what the Spirit does: cause you to walk in my statutes and be careful to obey my rules (the ESV notes, perhaps "my just decrees"). The old covenant gave the law on stone and left the people to obey it with hearts of stone. The new covenant writes the law on hearts of flesh and puts God's Spirit inside to move them to obey. Obedience is no longer a weight pressing from outside but a desire rising from within. Walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh (Gal 5:16).

When Nicodemus, a leading teacher of Israel, came to Jesus by night, Jesus told him, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God, and then rebuked him: Are you the teacher of Israel and yet you do not understand these things? (John 3:5, 10). Water and Spirit, a new birth from God — a teacher of Israel should have recognised the promise of Ezekiel 36.

Every true Christian has received this. Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him (Rom 8:9). And the evidence is a changed life: the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control (Gal 5:22-23). If you long to obey God and find yourself unable, the answer is not merely to try harder but to depend on the Spirit God has promised to put within you. It is God who works in you, both to will and to work for his good pleasure (Phil 2:13).

verseByVerse.quote: You shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers, and you shall be my people, and I will be your God. And I will deliver you from all your uncleannesses. And I will summon the grain and make it abundant and lay no famine upon you. I will make the fruit of the tree and the increase of the field abundant, that you may never again suffer the disgrace of famine among the nations.
verseByVerse.commentary:
You shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers, and you shall be my people, and I will be your God.

The covenant sentence again, now secure at last: you shall be my people, and I will be your God. What was always God's goal becomes a lived reality through a new heart and the indwelling Spirit.

And I will deliver you from all your uncleannesses. And I will summon the grain and make it abundant and lay no famine upon you. I will make the fruit of the tree and the increase of the field abundant, that you may never again suffer the disgrace of famine among the nations.

I will summon the grain — God speaks to the harvest as a master calls a servant. Inner renewal is followed by outward blessing. The land shares in the renewal of the people.

And I will deliver you from all your uncleannesses comes again, after the promise of a new heart. Cleansing is not a single moment only; God keeps cleansing the people he has made new. If we walk in the light... the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin (1 John 1:7).

verseByVerse.quote: Then you will remember your evil ways, and your deeds that were not good, and you will loathe yourselves for your iniquities and your abominations. It is not for your sake that I will act, declares the Lord GOD; let that be known to you. Be ashamed and confounded for your ways, O house of Israel.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then you will remember your evil ways, and your deeds that were not good, and you will loathe yourselves for your iniquities and your abominations.

Notice when this deep repentance happens: Then — after God has cleansed them, given them a new heart and blessed them. Grace does not make people careless about sin. It makes them hate it. The more clearly a person sees God's kindness, the more clearly they see how ugly their rebellion was.

That is a mark of genuine conversion. The forgiven do not shrug at their past. They grieve over it, not with despair, but with a humbled, grateful heart.

It is not for your sake that I will act, declares the Lord GOD; let that be known to you. Be ashamed and confounded for your ways, O house of Israel.

For the second time: It is not for your sake. God will not let his people take any credit for their salvation. Let that be known to you. The only boasting left is boasting in the Lord.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 33–38 — Like the Garden of Eden
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: On the day God cleanses them, the cities will be inhabited and the desolate land tilled (vv. 33-34), until people say, This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden (v. 35), and the nations will know that the LORD has rebuilt and replanted (v. 36). God will even let Israel ask him to multiply them like the flocks at Jerusalem's feasts (vv. 37-38).
verseByVerse.theology: God's cleansing leads to a restored creation, and his promises invite his people's prayers.

verseByVerse.quote: "Thus says the Lord GOD: On the day that I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I will cause the cities to be inhabited, and the waste places shall be rebuilt. And the land that was desolate shall be tilled, instead of being the desolation that it was in the sight of all who passed by. And they will say, 'This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden, and the waste and desolate and ruined cities are now fortified and inhabited.' Then the nations that are left all around you shall know that I am the LORD; I have rebuilt the ruined places and replanted that which was desolate. I am the LORD; I have spoken, and I will do it.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Thus says the Lord GOD: On the day that I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I will cause the cities to be inhabited, and the waste places shall be rebuilt.

On the day that I cleanse you. The rebuilding of the land flows from the cleansing of the people. Renewal always begins with forgiveness.

And the land that was desolate shall be tilled, instead of being the desolation that it was in the sight of all who passed by. And they will say, 'This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden, and the waste and desolate and ruined cities are now fortified and inhabited.'

Like the garden of Eden. The passers-by who once mocked the ruins will marvel at the transformation. Isaiah promised the same: he... makes her wilderness like Eden, her desert like the garden of the LORD (Isa 51:3). The Bible's story moves from Eden lost to Eden restored and surpassed: the river of the water of life, the tree of life, and leaves that were for the healing of the nations (Rev 22:1-2).

Then the nations that are left all around you shall know that I am the LORD; I have rebuilt the ruined places and replanted that which was desolate. I am the LORD; I have spoken, and I will do it.

I have spoken, and I will do it. The same signature that sealed the judgments now seals the promises. What God said about ruin came true. What he says about renewal will come true.

verseByVerse.quote: "Thus says the Lord GOD: This also I will let the house of Israel ask me to do for them: to increase their people like a flock. Like the flock for sacrifices, like the flock at Jerusalem during her appointed feasts, so shall the waste cities be filled with flocks of people. Then they will know that I am the LORD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Thus says the Lord GOD: This also I will let the house of Israel ask me to do for them: to increase their people like a flock.

Here is a lovely detail. Back in chapters 14 and 20 God refused to be inquired of by the elders. Now he says: This also I will let the house of Israel ask me to do for them. The door of prayer, closed by their sin, is opened again by his grace.

And notice: God has just promised to do this. Yet he invites them to ask for it. God's promises do not make prayer unnecessary. They make prayer confident. How much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him! (Matt 7:11). You do not have, because you do not ask (Jas 4:2).

Like the flock for sacrifices, like the flock at Jerusalem during her appointed feasts, so shall the waste cities be filled with flocks of people. Then they will know that I am the LORD."

Picture Jerusalem at Passover, the streets crowded with flocks of sheep brought for sacrifice (the ESV notes, literally "flock of holy things"). That is how full the empty cities will become — full of people, and full of people set apart to God.

A holy people, cleansed, given new hearts, filled with God's Spirit, crowding into God's presence. That is the church of Jesus Christ gathered from every nation — and it is the future of God's people in the new creation.

36.title: A New Heart and a New Spirit
36.overview:
Ezekiel prophesies to the mountains of Israel. The nations and Edom mocked the land, seized it with joy and contempt and made it a prey. God has spoken in his jealousy against them and swears that they will bear reproach (vv. 1-7).

But the mountains of Israel will put out branches and fruit for God's people, who will soon come home. God is for the land; it will be tilled and sown, its cities rebuilt and full of people and animals, and God will do more good than ever before. The land will no longer devour its people or bear the reproach of the nations (vv. 8-15).

Israel defiled the land with blood and idols, so God scattered them; but in exile they profaned his holy name, because the nations said the LORD's people had been driven from his land. So God will act, not for their sake, but for the sake of his holy name, and vindicate his holiness before the nations through them (vv. 16-23).

He will gather them home, sprinkle clean water on them and cleanse them from all their uncleanness and idols. He will give them a new heart and a new spirit, remove the heart of stone and give them a heart of flesh, and put his Spirit within them to make them walk in his ways. They will be his people and he their God, with abundant harvests. Then they will remember their ways and loathe themselves, knowing it was not for their sake (vv. 24-32).

On the day God cleanses them, the cities will be rebuilt and the desolate land tilled until people say it has become like the garden of Eden, and the nations will know that the LORD has rebuilt and replanted. God will let Israel ask him to multiply them like the sacrificial flocks at Jerusalem's feasts (vv. 33-38).
36.theology:
God is jealous for his people and his land, and does not let their enemies have the last word (vv. 5-7).

The God who was against his sinful people declares that he is for them, and his restoration exceeds what was lost (vv. 9, 11; Rom 8:31).

God's people profane his name when they fall, and he acts to vindicate his holiness (vv. 20-23; Rom 2:24).

Salvation rests not on the deserving of God's people but on the glory of God's name, which makes it certain (vv. 22, 32; Deut 9:4-6; Ps 115:1; Eph 2:8-9).

God cleanses his people, replaces their heart of stone with a heart of flesh, and puts his own Spirit within them to move them to obey — the new birth fulfilled in Christ (vv. 25-27; Deut 30:6; Jer 31:33; John 3:3-10; 1 Cor 6:11; Titus 3:5; Heb 10:22).

The Spirit's indwelling produces obedience from within (v. 27; Rom 8:9; Gal 5:16, 22-23; Phil 2:13).

Grace deepens repentance (v. 31).

Cleansing leads to a restored creation like Eden (vv. 33-36; Isa 51:3; Rev 22:1-2).

God's promises invite confident prayer (v. 37; Matt 7:11; Jas 4:2).
36.examples:
Mountains told to get ready, because the people are coming home.

Four words after years of judgment: I am for you.

Refugees who made the world ask what kind of God they had.

Not for your sake — and therefore certain.

Clean water sprinkled by God himself.

A heart transplant: stone out, flesh in.

God's own Spirit living inside.

A wasteland mistaken for Eden.

A promise God still invites you to ask for.

37.text: <sup>1</sup>The hand of the LORD was upon me, and he brought me out in the Spirit of the LORD and set me down in the middle of the valley; it was full of bones.<sup>2</sup>And he led me around among them, and behold, there were very many on the surface of the valley, and behold, they were very dry.<sup>3</sup>And he said to me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" And I answered, "O Lord GOD, you know."<sup>4</sup>Then he said to me, "Prophesy over these bones, and say to them, O dry bones, hear the word of the LORD.<sup>5</sup>Thus says the Lord GOD to these bones: Behold, I will cause breath to enter you, and you shall live.<sup>6</sup>And I will lay sinews upon you, and will cause flesh to come upon you, and cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and you shall live, and you shall know that I am the LORD."<sup>7</sup>So I prophesied as I was commanded. And as I prophesied, there was a sound, and behold, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to its bone.<sup>8</sup>And I looked, and behold, there were sinews on them, and flesh had come upon them, and skin had covered them. But there was no breath in them.<sup>9</sup>Then he said to me, "Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and say to the breath, Thus says the Lord GOD: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live."<sup>10</sup>So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived and stood on their feet, an exceedingly great army.<sup>11</sup>Then he said to me, "Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. Behold, they say, 'Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost; we are indeed cut off.'<sup>12</sup>Therefore prophesy, and say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I will open your graves and raise you from your graves, O my people. And I will bring you into the land of Israel.<sup>13</sup>And you shall know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves, and raise you from your graves, O my people.<sup>14</sup>And I will put my Spirit within you, and you shall live, and I will place you in your own land. Then you shall know that I am the LORD; I have spoken, and I will do it, declares the LORD."<sup>15</sup>The word of the LORD came to me:<sup>16</sup>"Son of man, take a stick and write on it, 'For Judah, and the people of Israel associated with him'; then take another stick and write on it, 'For Joseph (the stick of Ephraim) and all the house of Israel associated with him.'<sup>17</sup>And join them one to another into one stick, that they may become one in your hand.<sup>18</sup>And when your people say to you, 'Will you not tell us what you mean by these?'<sup>19</sup>say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am about to take the stick of Joseph (that is in the hand of Ephraim) and the tribes of Israel associated with him. And I will join with it the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, that they may be one in my hand.<sup>20</sup>When the sticks on which you write are in your hand before their eyes,<sup>21</sup>then say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I will take the people of Israel from the nations among which they have gone, and will gather them from all around, and bring them to their own land.<sup>22</sup>And I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel. And one king shall be king over them all, and they shall be no longer two nations, and no longer divided into two kingdoms.<sup>23</sup>They shall not defile themselves anymore with their idols and their detestable things, or with any of their transgressions.
