verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The Spirit sets Ezekiel down in a valley full of bones, very many and very dry (vv. 1-2). Son of man, can these bones live? He answers, O Lord GOD, you know (v. 3). He is told to prophesy to the bones that God will give them breath, sinews, flesh and skin, and they will live (vv. 4-6). As he prophesies there is a rattling; the bones come together and are covered with flesh, but there is no breath (vv. 7-8). Then he prophesies to the breath, Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live, and they stand up, an exceedingly great army (vv. 9-10).
verseByVerse.theology: God gives life to the dead through his word and his Spirit.

verseByVerse.quote: The hand of the LORD was upon me, and he brought me out in the Spirit of the LORD and set me down in the middle of the valley; it was full of bones. And he led me around among them, and behold, there were very many on the surface of the valley, and behold, they were very dry.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The hand of the LORD was upon me, and he brought me out in the Spirit of the LORD and set me down in the middle of the valley; it was full of bones.

This is a well-known vision, and it begins with a horrifying scene. Ezekiel is set down in a valley (the ESV notes, perhaps "plain") full of bones. Picture an old battlefield where no one ever buried the dead.

And he led me around among them, and behold, there were very many on the surface of the valley, and behold, they were very dry.

God does not let Ezekiel glance and look away. He led me around among them. He walks through the whole field. Two things strike him: very many, and very dry. These are not people recently dead. They have been lying in the sun so long that nothing is left but bleached bone. Every trace of life is gone.

That is the point. This is not a sick patient who might recover. It is death at its most final. Whatever happens next cannot be explained by natural recovery.

verseByVerse.quote: And he said to me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" And I answered, "O Lord GOD, you know."
verseByVerse.commentary:
And he said to me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" And I answered, "O Lord GOD, you know."

God asks a question that seems absurd. Can these bones live? Every human answer is obviously no.

Ezekiel's answer is a model of faith: O Lord GOD, you know. He does not say yes, because he cannot see how. He does not say no, because he knows who is asking. He puts the impossible back into the hands of the only one who knows what is possible.

Many believers stand in valleys like this. A marriage that seems dead. A child who has walked away from God. A church where nothing spiritual seems to be happening. A nation far from God. A heart that feels completely dry. The honest answer to "Can this live?" is often: not by any power I have. The faithful answer is: O Lord GOD, you know. Abraham believed in the God... who gives life to the dead and calls into existence the things that do not exist (Rom 4:17).

verseByVerse.quote: Then he said to me, "Prophesy over these bones, and say to them, O dry bones, hear the word of the LORD. Thus says the Lord GOD to these bones: Behold, I will cause breath to enter you, and you shall live. And I will lay sinews upon you, and will cause flesh to come upon you, and cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and you shall live, and you shall know that I am the LORD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then he said to me, "Prophesy over these bones, and say to them, O dry bones, hear the word of the LORD.

Now God gives Ezekiel a strange preaching assignment even for him: preach to a field of skeletons. O dry bones, hear the word of the LORD.

It looks ridiculous. Dead bones cannot hear. But that is exactly the situation of every preacher of the gospel. Paul says we were all dead in the trespasses and sins (Eph 2:1). Preaching to people who are spiritually dead only makes sense if God's word carries God's power. And it does: faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ (Rom 10:17). We have been born again through the living and abiding word of God (1 Pet 1:23).

Thus says the Lord GOD to these bones: Behold, I will cause breath to enter you, and you shall live.

And I will lay sinews upon you, and will cause flesh to come upon you, and cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and you shall live, and you shall know that I am the LORD."

Every verb has God as its subject: I will cause breath... I will lay sinews... cause flesh... cover you... put breath in you. The preacher speaks; God acts.

The ESV notes that breath may also be rendered "spirit", here and all through this passage. Hold on to that; it becomes the key to the whole vision.

verseByVerse.quote: So I prophesied as I was commanded. And as I prophesied, there was a sound, and behold, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to its bone. And I looked, and behold, there were sinews on them, and flesh had come upon them, and skin had covered them. But there was no breath in them.
verseByVerse.commentary:
So I prophesied as I was commanded. And as I prophesied, there was a sound, and behold, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to its bone.

Ezekiel obeys. And while he is still speaking, there is a noise (the ESV notes, perhaps "an earthquake") — a rattling across the valley as thousands of bones scrape and click and slide toward each other, bone to its bone. Each finds its right place.

Imagine standing there as the scattered skeletons assemble themselves. God's word does not merely inform. It does things.

And I looked, and behold, there were sinews on them, and flesh had come upon them, and skin had covered them. But there was no breath in them.

Sinews, flesh, skin — the valley now looks like a field of fallen soldiers, whole and intact. But there was no breath in them.

That is a sobering stage. Bodies that look complete but have no life. It is possible for a person, or a church, to have all the right structure — doctrine, organisation, activity, respectability — and no breath. Reformation of the outside is not the same as life. Something more is needed.

verseByVerse.quote: Then he said to me, "Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and say to the breath, Thus says the Lord GOD: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live." So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived and stood on their feet, an exceedingly great army.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then he said to me, "Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and say to the breath, Thus says the Lord GOD: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live."

So God tells Ezekiel to prophesy again — this time not to the bones but to the breath. Come from the four winds, O breath. The ESV notes that breath here too may be "spirit". From every direction the life-giving breath is summoned.

The picture goes back to creation. God formed the man of dust from the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living creature (Gen 2:7). Only the breath of God turns a body into a living person. Here is a second creation.

And it points forward. On the evening of his resurrection, Jesus stood among his frightened disciples, breathed on them and said to them, "Receive the Holy Spirit" (John 20:22). The breath of God that raised the dead bones is the Spirit whom the risen Christ gives.

So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived and stood on their feet, an exceedingly great army.

They lived and stood on their feet. The valley of death becomes a vast living army. An exceedingly great army.

This is how God works. Word and Spirit together. The preacher speaks God's word; God's Spirit breathes life. Neither is enough alone: words without the Spirit leave corpses; and the Spirit ordinarily works through the word. At Pentecost Peter preached and the Spirit moved, and there were added that day about three thousand souls (Acts 2:41). A valley of bones stood up.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 11–14 — I Will Open Your Graves
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: These bones are the whole house of Israel, who say, Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost; we are indeed cut off (v. 11). God answers, Behold, I will open your graves and raise you from your graves, O my people, and bring you home (vv. 12-13). And I will put my Spirit within you, and you shall live (v. 14).
verseByVerse.theology: God's answer to hopelessness is resurrection by his Spirit.

verseByVerse.quote: Then he said to me, "Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. Behold, they say, 'Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost; we are indeed cut off.'
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then he said to me, "Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. Behold, they say, 'Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost; we are indeed cut off.'

Now God explains the vision. These bones are the whole house of Israel. And he quotes what the exiles were actually saying: Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost; we are indeed cut off.

That is the voice of despair. After Jerusalem fell, the exiles felt like a nation that had died. The temple was gone, the king was gone, the land was gone. They felt as dead as bleached bones — cut off from God and from any future.

Many people feel exactly that. Our hope is lost. After a devastating loss, a moral collapse, years of prayer that seem unanswered. God does not rebuke the exiles for saying it. He answers it.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore prophesy, and say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I will open your graves and raise you from your graves, O my people. And I will bring you into the land of Israel. And you shall know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves, and raise you from your graves, O my people. And I will put my Spirit within you, and you shall live, and I will place you in your own land. Then you shall know that I am the LORD; I have spoken, and I will do it, declares the LORD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
Therefore prophesy, and say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I will open your graves and raise you from your graves, O my people. And I will bring you into the land of Israel.

The image shifts from a valley to graves, and the promise becomes explicit: I will open your graves and raise you from your graves. God will bring the "dead" nation back to life and back to its land.

And notice the tender phrase, twice: O my people. They thought they were cut off. God calls them his.

And you shall know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves, and raise you from your graves, O my people.

And I will put my Spirit within you, and you shall live, and I will place you in your own land. Then you shall know that I am the LORD; I have spoken, and I will do it, declares the LORD."

And here is the key that the ESV's note prepared us for: the breath of the vision is my Spirit. I will put my Spirit within you, and you shall live. It is the promise of 36:27 again. National restoration and spiritual rebirth are both the work of God's Spirit.

This vision's first meaning is the return of Israel from exile. But Scripture shows its fuller meaning. It is a picture of the new birth: you, who were dead in your trespasses... God made alive together with him (Col 2:13). And it points to the final resurrection of the body. Jesus said, an hour is coming when all who are in the tombs will hear his voice and come out (John 5:28-29). Isaiah had said, Your dead shall live; their bodies shall rise (Isa 26:19). And Paul: If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit (Rom 8:11).

At the heart of it all is the one who said, I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live (John 11:25). He went down into a grave himself, and on the third day God opened it. Because his grave was opened, every believer's grave will be opened too. No valley is too dry for him.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Ezekiel writes For Judah on one stick and For Joseph (Ephraim) on another, and joins them into one in his hand (vv. 15-17). When the people ask what it means (v. 18), God explains that he will join the divided kingdoms into one (vv. 19-20), gather them home and make them one nation under one king (vv. 21-22), cleansed from their idols: they shall be my people, and I will be their God (v. 23).
verseByVerse.theology: God heals the divisions of his people and makes them one under one King.

verseByVerse.quote: The word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, take a stick and write on it, 'For Judah, and the people of Israel associated with him'; then take another stick and write on it, 'For Joseph (the stick of Ephraim) and all the house of Israel associated with him.' And join them one to another into one stick, that they may become one in your hand.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, take a stick and write on it, 'For Judah, and the people of Israel associated with him'; then take another stick and write on it, 'For Joseph (the stick of Ephraim) and all the house of Israel associated with him.'

A new sign, simple and vivid. Two sticks (the ESV notes, perhaps "one piece of wood" each). On one Ezekiel writes For Judah, the southern kingdom. On the other, For Joseph (the stick of Ephraim) — the northern kingdom, led by the tribe of Ephraim.

For more than three centuries God's people had been split in two. It began when the northern tribes rejected David's grandson: What portion do we have in David?... To your tents, O Israel! (1 Kgs 12:16). Two kingdoms, two kings, rival shrines, and often war between brothers.

And join them one to another into one stick, that they may become one in your hand.

Ezekiel holds the two sticks end to end in his hand, so that they look like one. That they may become one in your hand.

verseByVerse.quote: And when your people say to you, 'Will you not tell us what you mean by these?' say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am about to take the stick of Joseph (that is in the hand of Ephraim) and the tribes of Israel associated with him. And I will join with it the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, that they may be one in my hand. When the sticks on which you write are in your hand before their eyes, then say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I will take the people of Israel from the nations among which they have gone, and will gather them from all around, and bring them to their own land. And I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel. And one king shall be king over them all, and they shall be no longer two nations, and no longer divided into two kingdoms. They shall not defile themselves anymore with their idols and their detestable things, or with any of their transgressions. But I will save them from all the backslidings in which they have sinned, and will cleanse them; and they shall be my people, and I will be their God.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And when your people say to you, 'Will you not tell us what you mean by these?'

say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am about to take the stick of Joseph (that is in the hand of Ephraim) and the tribes of Israel associated with him. And I will join with it the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, that they may be one in my hand.

One in my hand. Ezekiel's hand is a picture of God's hand. Only God can make a divided people one. (The ESV notes the Hebrew is literally "And I will place them on it, the stick of Judah".)

When the sticks on which you write are in your hand before their eyes, then say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I will take the people of Israel from the nations among which they have gone, and will gather them from all around, and bring them to their own land.

And I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel. And one king shall be king over them all, and they shall be no longer two nations, and no longer divided into two kingdoms.

The resurrection of the bones leads to the reunion of the tribes. One nation... one king... no longer two. Division among God's people is a wound that God himself will heal.

Jesus prayed for the same unity in the church: that they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me, and I in you (John 17:21). And at the cross he did something even greater than joining Judah and Ephraim: he joined Jew and Gentile, that he might create in himself one new man in place of the two, so making peace (Eph 2:15). You are all one in Christ Jesus (Gal 3:28).

Churches divided by pride, personalities and old grudges should hear this sign. The unity God gives is real, and it comes from being held in one hand.

They shall not defile themselves anymore with their idols and their detestable things, or with any of their transgressions. But I will save them from all the backslidings in which they have sinned, and will cleanse them; and they shall be my people, and I will be their God.

And the unity is a holy unity. The idols that divided them will be gone. God will save them from all the backslidings (the ESV notes that other manuscripts read "dwellings") and cleanse them. True unity is not agreeing to overlook sin together; it is being cleansed together and belonging to God together.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 24–28 — My Dwelling Place with Them
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: My servant David shall be king over them, and they shall all have one shepherd (v. 24), and they will live in the land forever with David as prince forever (v. 25). God will make a covenant of peace, an everlasting covenant, and set my sanctuary in their midst forevermore (v. 26). My dwelling place shall be with them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people (v. 27), and the nations will know that he sanctifies Israel (v. 28).
verseByVerse.theology: The goal of all God's work is his everlasting presence with a people united under his King.

verseByVerse.quote: "My servant David shall be king over them, and they shall all have one shepherd. They shall walk in my rules and be careful to obey my statutes. They shall dwell in the land that I gave to my servant Jacob, where your fathers lived. They and their children and their children's children shall dwell there forever, and David my servant shall be their prince forever.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"My servant David shall be king over them, and they shall all have one shepherd. They shall walk in my rules and be careful to obey my statutes.

Who is the one king of verse 22? My servant David — the promised King of David's line we met in 34:23-24. One shepherd for one flock. Jesus said, there will be one flock, one shepherd (John 10:16).

And under this King, God's people shall walk in my rules. The unity and the obedience both come from having one King.

They shall dwell in the land that I gave to my servant Jacob, where your fathers lived. They and their children and their children's children shall dwell there forever, and David my servant shall be their prince forever.

Again and again: forever (vv. 25, 26, 28). The land forever, the generations forever, David's reign forever. No human king could be prince forever. Only the one of whom the angel said, he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end (Luke 1:33).

verseByVerse.quote: I will make a covenant of peace with them. It shall be an everlasting covenant with them. And I will set them in their land and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in their midst forevermore. My dwelling place shall be with them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD who sanctifies Israel, when my sanctuary is in their midst forevermore."
verseByVerse.commentary:
I will make a covenant of peace with them. It shall be an everlasting covenant with them. And I will set them in their land and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in their midst forevermore.

A covenant of peace... an everlasting covenant. The covenant of 34:25 and the everlasting covenant of 16:60 are the same. It will never be broken, because it rests on God. (The ESV notes that the Hebrew lacks in their land.)

And the climax: and will set my sanctuary in their midst forevermore. The book began with the glory leaving the sanctuary (chs. 10-11). It is moving toward the glory returning (ch. 43). The whole point of restoration is not land or prosperity. It is God living among his people again.

My dwelling place shall be with them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

My dwelling place shall be with them. Paul quotes this promise to the church: we are the temple of the living God; as God said, "I will make my dwelling among them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people" (2 Cor 6:16). And John heard it announced from the throne at the end of all things: Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man. He will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God (Rev 21:3).

Between Ezekiel and Revelation stands Jesus: the Word became flesh and dwelt among us (John 1:14). God's dwelling with his people came in a person before it came in a city.

Then the nations will know that I am the LORD who sanctifies Israel, when my sanctuary is in their midst forevermore."

The LORD who sanctifies Israel. God's presence makes his people holy. And the nations watching will know it. A people raised from the dead, made one, cleansed, and indwelt by God — that is the testimony the world needs to see.

The valley of dry bones ends in a sanctuary. Death gives way to life, division to unity, exile to home, and absence to presence. That is the story of the gospel, and it is the destination of every believer.

37.title: Can These Bones Live?
37.overview:
The Spirit of the LORD sets Ezekiel down in a valley full of very many, very dry bones. God asks whether these bones can live, and Ezekiel answers that God knows. He is told to prophesy to the bones that God will give them breath, sinews, flesh and skin. As he prophesies, the bones rattle together and are covered with flesh, but they have no breath. Then he prophesies to the breath to come from the four winds, and breath enters them; they live and stand up, a vast army (vv. 1-10).

God explains that the bones are the whole house of Israel, who say their bones are dried up, their hope is lost and they are cut off. God promises to open their graves, raise them up, bring them home, and put his Spirit within them so that they live (vv. 11-14).

Ezekiel takes two sticks, writes Judah on one and Joseph (Ephraim) on the other, and joins them into one in his hand. God explains that he will gather his people from the nations and make them one nation in the land under one king, no longer divided into two kingdoms, cleansed from their idols; they will be his people and he their God (vv. 15-23).

God's servant David will be king and one shepherd over them; they will obey God and live in the land forever with David as their prince forever. God will make an everlasting covenant of peace with them and set his sanctuary among them forever. His dwelling place will be with them, and the nations will know that the LORD sanctifies Israel (vv. 24-28).
37.theology:
God can give life where every human hope is gone; faith answers the impossible with, O Lord GOD, you know (vv. 1-3; Rom 4:17).

God gives life through his word and his Spirit together; outward form without the Spirit is still death (vv. 4-10; Gen 2:7; Rom 10:17; 1 Pet 1:23; John 20:22; Acts 2:41).

God answers his people's despair with the promise of resurrection by his Spirit (vv. 11-14).

The vision's promise reaches to the new birth and to the bodily resurrection, secured by Christ, the resurrection and the life (Col 2:13; John 5:28-29; 11:25; Rom 8:11; Isa 26:19).

God heals the divisions of his people and makes them one under one King, in holiness (vv. 15-23; John 17:21; Eph 2:15-16; Gal 3:28).

The promised David is Christ, the one shepherd who reigns forever (vv. 24-25; 34:23-24; John 10:16; Luke 1:32-33).

The goal of redemption is God's everlasting dwelling with his people, fulfilled in Christ, the church and the new creation (vv. 26-28; John 1:14; 2 Cor 6:16; Rev 21:3).
37.examples:
A battlefield of bleached bones no one buried.

A question with only one honest answer: you know.

Preaching to skeletons.

The rattle of bones finding their places.

Bodies complete, and no breath.

Breath from the four winds, and an army standing up.

Our hope is lost — and God opening graves.

Two sticks held as one.

My dwelling place shall be with them.

In the latter years you will go against the land that is restored from war, the land whose people were gathered from many peoples upon the mountains of Israel, which had been a continual waste. Its people were brought out from the peoples and now dwell securely, all of them.<sup>9</sup>You will advance, coming on like a storm. I will fall upon the quiet people who dwell securely, all of them dwelling without walls, and having no bars or gates,'<sup>12</sup>to seize spoil and carry off plunder, to turn your hand against the waste places that are now inhabited, and the people who were gathered from the nations, who have acquired livestock and goods, who dwell at the center of the earth.<sup>13</sup>Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish and all its leaders will say to you, 'Have you come to seize spoil? Have you assembled your hosts to carry off plunder, to carry away silver and gold, to take away livestock and goods, to seize great spoil?'<sup>14</sup>"Therefore, son of man, prophesy, and say to Gog, Thus says the Lord GOD: On that day when my people Israel are dwelling securely, will you not know it?<sup>15</sup>You will come from your place out of the uttermost parts of the north, you and many peoples with you, all of them riding on horses, a great host, a mighty army.<sup>16</sup>You will come up against my people Israel, like a cloud covering the land. In the latter days I will bring you against my land, that the nations may know me, when through you, O Gog, I vindicate my holiness before their eyes.<sup>17</sup>"Thus says the Lord GOD: Are you he of whom I spoke in former days by my servants the prophets of Israel, who in those days prophesied for years that I would bring you against them?<sup>18</sup>But on that day, the day that Gog shall come against the land of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, my wrath will be roused in my anger.<sup>19</sup>For in my jealousy and in my blazing wrath I declare, On that day there shall be a great earthquake in the land of Israel.<sup>20</sup>The fish of the sea and the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the field and all creeping things that creep on the ground, and all the people who are on the face of the earth, shall quake at my presence. And the mountains shall be thrown down, and the cliffs shall fall, and every wall shall tumble to the ground.<sup>21</sup>I will summon a sword against Gog on all my mountains, declares the Lord GOD. Every man's sword will be against his brother.<sup>22</sup>With pestilence and bloodshed I will enter into judgment with him, and I will rain upon him and his hordes and the many peoples who are with him torrential rains and hailstones, fire and sulfur.<sup>23</sup>So I will show my greatness and my holiness and make myself known in the eyes of many nations. Then they will know that I am the LORD.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Ezekiel prophesies against Gog, of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal (v. 2). God will turn him about with hooks in his jaws and bring him out with a vast armed host, joined by Persia, Cush, Put, Gomer and Beth-togarmah (vv. 3-7). In the latter years he will come against the land restored from war, whose people dwell securely, like a storm and a cloud covering the land (vv. 8-9).
verseByVerse.theology: Even the most fearsome enemy of God's people moves only by God's hook in its jaw.

verseByVerse.quote: The word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, set your face toward Gog, of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him and say, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. And I will turn you about and put hooks into your jaws, and I will bring you out, and all your army, horses and horsemen, all of them clothed in full armor, a great host, all of them with buckler and shield, wielding swords. Persia, Cush, and Put are with them, all of them with shield and helmet; Gomer and all his hordes; Beth-togarmah from the uttermost parts of the north with all his hordes— many peoples are with you.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, set your face toward Gog, of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him

Chapters 38 and 39 are much debated. After the promises of restoration in chapters 34-37 — a new Shepherd, a new heart, dry bones living, God dwelling with his people — comes a final enemy: Gog, of the land of Magog.

Who is Gog? No historical king by this name is known with certainty. Magog, Meshech, Tubal and Gomer appear in Genesis as descendants of Japheth (Gen 10:2), peoples on the far northern edges of Israel's known world. The ESV notes that chief prince of Meshech may be rendered "prince of Rosh, Meshech"; some have tried to link Rosh or Meshech with modern nations, but the text itself gives no such identification, and such readings go beyond what Ezekiel says.

Faithful Christians have read these chapters in different ways. Some understand them as a literal future invasion of a restored Israel in the last days. Others read them as a symbolic picture of the final, all-out assault of evil against God's people at the end of history — a reading supported by the fact that Revelation takes up the names Gog and Magog for the nations gathered against the camp of the saints and the beloved city just before the end (Rev 20:8-9). Whatever the details, the main message is clear and shared: however great the last enemy, God will destroy it and protect his people.

and say, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. And I will turn you about and put hooks into your jaws, and I will bring you out, and all your army, horses and horsemen, all of them clothed in full armor, a great host, all of them with buckler and shield, wielding swords.

I will... put hooks into your jaws, and I will bring you out. The same picture used of Pharaoh (29:4). Gog thinks he is attacking on his own initiative. In fact God is leading him like an animal on a hook. The mightiest enemy moves only as God allows.

Persia, Cush, and Put are with them, all of them with shield and helmet; Gomer and all his hordes; Beth-togarmah from the uttermost parts of the north with all his hordes— many peoples are with you.

The coalition comes from every direction: Persia in the east, Cush and Put in the south, Gomer and Beth-togarmah in the far north. It is a picture of the whole world gathering against God's people.

verseByVerse.quote: "Be ready and keep ready, you and all your hosts that are assembled about you, and be a guard for them. After many days you will be mustered. In the latter years you will go against the land that is restored from war, the land whose people were gathered from many peoples upon the mountains of Israel, which had been a continual waste. Its people were brought out from the peoples and now dwell securely, all of them. You will advance, coming on like a storm. You will be like a cloud covering the land, you and all your hordes, and many peoples with you.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Be ready and keep ready, you and all your hosts that are assembled about you, and be a guard for them.

There is irony in this command. God tells Gog to get ready. Make your preparations. Muster your armies. It will make no difference.

After many days you will be mustered. In the latter years you will go against the land that is restored from war, the land whose people were gathered from many peoples upon the mountains of Israel, which had been a continual waste. Its people were brought out from the peoples and now dwell securely, all of them.

After many days... In the latter years. This attack comes after the restoration of chapters 34-37. God's people are gathered, the land rebuilt, and they dwell securely. It is precisely when God's people are at peace that the final enemy strikes.

You will advance, coming on like a storm. You will be like a cloud covering the land, you and all your hordes, and many peoples with you.

Like a storm... like a cloud covering the land. The threat is overwhelming. The New Testament does not promise believers that the world will grow friendlier before the end. Jesus said, In the world you will have tribulation. But take heart; I have overcome the world (John 16:33).

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Gog will devise an evil plan to attack the quiet people who dwell securely, all of them dwelling without walls, to plunder them (vv. 10-12). The traders of Sheba, Dedan and Tarshish ask whether he has come for plunder (v. 13). He will come from the far north against God's people, that the nations may know me, when through you, O Gog, I vindicate my holiness before their eyes (vv. 14-16).
verseByVerse.theology: The enemy's schemes against God's people serve God's purpose to reveal his holiness.

verseByVerse.quote: "Thus says the Lord GOD: On that day, thoughts will come into your mind, and you will devise an evil scheme and say, 'I will go up against the land of unwalled villages. I will fall upon the quiet people who dwell securely, all of them dwelling without walls, and having no bars or gates,' to seize spoil and carry off plunder, to turn your hand against the waste places that are now inhabited, and the people who were gathered from the nations, who have acquired livestock and goods, who dwell at the center of the earth. Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish and all its leaders will say to you, 'Have you come to seize spoil? Have you assembled your hosts to carry off plunder, to carry away silver and gold, to take away livestock and goods, to seize great spoil?'
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Thus says the Lord GOD: On that day, thoughts will come into your mind, and you will devise an evil scheme

God has hooked Gog's jaw, and yet Gog's own mind devises an evil scheme. Both are true: God is sovereign over the attack, and Gog is guilty for his wicked intent. It is the same pattern as the cross, where Jesus was delivered up according to the definite plan and foreknowledge of God and killed by the hands of lawless men (Acts 2:23).

and say, 'I will go up against the land of unwalled villages. I will fall upon the quiet people who dwell securely, all of them dwelling without walls, and having no bars or gates,'

Gog's target is a people who have no walls, no bars, no gates. They look defenceless. In fact they have something better than walls: God himself. The gates of hell shall not prevail against Christ's church (Matt 16:18).

to seize spoil and carry off plunder, to turn your hand against the waste places that are now inhabited, and the people who were gathered from the nations, who have acquired livestock and goods, who dwell at the center of the earth.

Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish and all its leaders will say to you, 'Have you come to seize spoil? Have you assembled your hosts to carry off plunder, to carry away silver and gold, to take away livestock and goods, to seize great spoil?'

Gog's motive is greed. The world's traders watch and ask the obvious question: are you here for plunder? (The ESV notes that leaders is literally "young lions".) Hostility to God's people is often mixed with simple covetousness.

verseByVerse.quote: "Therefore, son of man, prophesy, and say to Gog, Thus says the Lord GOD: On that day when my people Israel are dwelling securely, will you not know it? You will come from your place out of the uttermost parts of the north, you and many peoples with you, all of them riding on horses, a great host, a mighty army. You will come up against my people Israel, like a cloud covering the land. In the latter days I will bring you against my land, that the nations may know me, when through you, O Gog, I vindicate my holiness before their eyes.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Therefore, son of man, prophesy, and say to Gog, Thus says the Lord GOD: On that day when my people Israel are dwelling securely, will you not know it?

You will come from your place out of the uttermost parts of the north, you and many peoples with you, all of them riding on horses, a great host, a mighty army. You will come up against my people Israel, like a cloud covering the land.

My people Israel. Gog attacks a people God calls his own. To attack them is to attack him.

In the latter days I will bring you against my land, that the nations may know me, when through you, O Gog, I vindicate my holiness before their eyes.

Here is the purpose of the whole invasion: that the nations may know me. God brings Gog so that through you, O Gog, I vindicate my holiness before their eyes. In 36:23 God vindicated his holiness through restoring Israel. Here he vindicates it through destroying Israel's last enemy.

That is a remarkable perspective on evil. Even the fiercest opposition to God's people ends up serving the display of God's glory. Why do the nations rage...? He who sits in the heavens laughs (Ps 2:1, 4).

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: God asks whether Gog is the one the earlier prophets spoke of (v. 17). When Gog comes, God's wrath will be roused: a great earthquake will shake all creation, mountains and walls will fall (vv. 18-20), the invaders will turn their swords on one another, and God will judge them with pestilence, blood, hail, fire and sulfur (vv. 21-22). So I will show my greatness and my holiness and make myself known in the eyes of many nations (v. 23).
verseByVerse.theology: At the climax of evil's assault, God himself fights for his people and makes himself known to the nations.

verseByVerse.quote: "Thus says the Lord GOD: Are you he of whom I spoke in former days by my servants the prophets of Israel, who in those days prophesied for years that I would bring you against them? But on that day, the day that Gog shall come against the land of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, my wrath will be roused in my anger. For in my jealousy and in my blazing wrath I declare, On that day there shall be a great earthquake in the land of Israel. The fish of the sea and the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the field and all creeping things that creep on the ground, and all the people who are on the face of the earth, shall quake at my presence. And the mountains shall be thrown down, and the cliffs shall fall, and every wall shall tumble to the ground.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Thus says the Lord GOD: Are you he of whom I spoke in former days by my servants the prophets of Israel, who in those days prophesied for years that I would bring you against them?

God suggests that Gog is the fulfilment of what earlier prophets had spoken of — the final gathering of the nations against God's people. Zephaniah said God would gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour out upon them my indignation (Zeph 3:8). Zechariah spoke of all the nations against Jerusalem, and then the LORD will go out and fight against those nations (Zech 14:2-3).

But on that day, the day that Gog shall come against the land of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, my wrath will be roused in my anger.

For in my jealousy and in my blazing wrath I declare, On that day there shall be a great earthquake in the land of Israel.

The fish of the sea and the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the field and all creeping things that creep on the ground, and all the people who are on the face of the earth, shall quake at my presence. And the mountains shall be thrown down, and the cliffs shall fall, and every wall shall tumble to the ground.

When God rises to defend his people, all creation shakes. Fish, birds, animals, people, mountains, cliffs, walls. It is the language of the final shaking of the world. Hebrews speaks of it: Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heavens, so that the things that cannot be shaken may remain (Heb 12:26-27). Everything that is not God's will fall. God's people will stand.

verseByVerse.quote: I will summon a sword against Gog on all my mountains, declares the Lord GOD. Every man's sword will be against his brother. With pestilence and bloodshed I will enter into judgment with him, and I will rain upon him and his hordes and the many peoples who are with him torrential rains and hailstones, fire and sulfur. So I will show my greatness and my holiness and make myself known in the eyes of many nations. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
I will summon a sword against Gog on all my mountains, declares the Lord GOD. Every man's sword will be against his brother.

The invading army turns on itself. Every man's sword will be against his brother (the ESV notes, literally "against him"). God had done this before, in Jehoshaphat's day, when the invading armies all helped to destroy one another and Judah did not have to fight (2 Chr 20:23). Evil is not only defeated by God; it is often self-destructive.

With pestilence and bloodshed I will enter into judgment with him, and I will rain upon him and his hordes and the many peoples who are with him torrential rains and hailstones, fire and sulfur.

Hailstones, fire and sulfur — the weapons of heaven, reminiscent of Sodom and the plagues of Egypt. God's people do not win this battle. God does. At the end, Revelation says of Gog and Magog: fire came down from heaven and consumed them (Rev 20:9).

So I will show my greatness and my holiness and make myself known in the eyes of many nations. Then they will know that I am the LORD.

And the goal once more: make myself known in the eyes of many nations. The whole of history is heading toward the day when every nation knows who the LORD is. The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ, and he shall reign forever and ever (Rev 11:15).

For Christians, this chapter is not a code for predicting headlines. It is an assurance. However powerful the forces that gather against Christ's people — in any age, and at the end — they move only by God's hook, they serve God's purposes, and they will fall. He who is in you is greater than he who is in the world (1 John 4:4).

38.title: Gog of the Land of Magog
38.overview:
Ezekiel prophesies against Gog, of the land of Magog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. God declares that he is against Gog and will lead him out, as with hooks in his jaws, with a vast armed host and allies from Persia, Cush, Put, Gomer and Beth-togarmah. In the latter years Gog will come like a storm against the restored land, whose people have been gathered from the nations and now live securely (vv. 1-9).

Gog will devise an evil scheme to attack these unwalled villages and seize plunder, while the traders of the nations ask whether he has come for spoil. He will come from the far north against God's people, and through him God will vindicate his holiness before the nations (vv. 10-16).

God asks whether Gog is the one the earlier prophets foretold. When Gog attacks, God's wrath will be roused: a great earthquake will shake all creation, the invaders will turn on one another, and God will judge them with pestilence, bloodshed, hail, fire and sulfur, showing his greatness and holiness to many nations (vv. 17-23).

Christians have read these chapters either as a future literal invasion of a restored Israel or as a symbolic picture of the final assault of evil on God's people, taken up in Revelation 20. Both readings share the central message: God is sovereign over the last enemy and will destroy it to protect his people and reveal his glory.
38.theology:
The fiercest enemies of God's people move only as God allows, yet remain guilty for their evil schemes (vv. 4, 10; Acts 2:23).

God's people may face their greatest assault even after restoration, but they are not defenceless (vv. 8-12; John 16:33; Matt 16:18).

God turns the rage of the nations into an occasion to vindicate his holiness and make himself known (vv. 16, 23; Ps 2:1-6).

God himself fights for his people at the climax of history, shaking all creation so that only what cannot be shaken remains (vv. 18-22; Zech 14:2-3; Heb 12:26-28; Rev 20:7-10).

The purpose of these chapters is assurance, not speculation: he who is in believers is greater than he who is in the world (1 John 4:4).
38.examples:
A mighty warlord led by a hook in his jaw.

An army gathering from every point of the compass.

Unwalled villages that turn out to be unconquerable.

Traders watching and asking: are you here for the plunder?

Fish, birds and mountains trembling.

An army turning its swords on itself.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–8 — Gog Falls on the Mountains of Israel
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: God is against Gog and will drive him to the mountains of Israel (vv. 1-2), strike the bow from his hand and the arrows from the other (v. 3), and make him fall on the open field as food for birds and beasts (vv. 4-5). Fire will fall on Magog and the coastlands (v. 6). And my holy name I will make known in the midst of my people Israel, and I will not let my holy name be profaned anymore (v. 7). Behold, it is coming and it will be brought about (v. 8).
verseByVerse.theology: God will end every assault on his people and never again let his name be profaned.

verseByVerse.quote: "And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. And I will turn you about and drive you forward, and bring you up from the uttermost parts of the north, and lead you against the mountains of Israel. Then I will strike your bow from your left hand, and will make your arrows drop out of your right hand. You shall fall on the mountains of Israel, you and all your hordes and the peoples who are with you. I will give you to birds of prey of every sort and to the beasts of the field to be devoured. You shall fall in the open field, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD. I will send fire on Magog and on those who dwell securely in the coastlands, and they shall know that I am the LORD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.

Chapter 39 retells the fall of Gog in more detail, as if zooming in on the battlefield. (Once more the ESV notes the alternative "prince of Rosh, Meshech".)

And I will turn you about and drive you forward, and bring you up from the uttermost parts of the north, and lead you against the mountains of Israel.

Drive you forward — the ESV notes it may be "drag you along". Gog comes because God brings him. He is walking into a trap God has set.

Then I will strike your bow from your left hand, and will make your arrows drop out of your right hand.

A simple, vivid picture. The archer raises his bow, and it is struck from his hand; his arrows fall to the ground. God disarms the enemy before a single arrow flies. He breaks the bow and shatters the spear (Ps 46:9).

You shall fall on the mountains of Israel, you and all your hordes and the peoples who are with you. I will give you to birds of prey of every sort and to the beasts of the field to be devoured. You shall fall in the open field, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.

The invader who came to plunder the mountains of Israel falls on them. The one who meant to devour becomes food.

I will send fire on Magog and on those who dwell securely in the coastlands, and they shall know that I am the LORD.

Judgment reaches back to Gog's own homeland and to those who dwell securely in the coastlands — the distant nations who thought themselves safe. There is no security anywhere apart from God.

verseByVerse.quote: "And my holy name I will make known in the midst of my people Israel, and I will not let my holy name be profaned anymore. And the nations shall know that I am the LORD, the Holy One in Israel. Behold, it is coming and it will be brought about, declares the Lord GOD. That is the day of which I have spoken.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"And my holy name I will make known in the midst of my people Israel, and I will not let my holy name be profaned anymore. And the nations shall know that I am the LORD, the Holy One in Israel.

Here is the heart of the chapter. I will not let my holy name be profaned anymore. Israel's sin had profaned God's name among the nations (36:20). The nations' attack could have profaned it again. God will not allow it. His name will be known as holy both in the midst of my people and among the nations.

Behold, it is coming and it will be brought about, declares the Lord GOD. That is the day of which I have spoken.

It is coming and it will be brought about. The final victory of God is not uncertain. It is the day of which I have spoken. However long the conflict between God's kingdom and the powers of evil seems, its outcome is already settled.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 9–16 — Burning the Weapons, Burying the Dead
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Israel will burn the enemy's weapons as fuel for seven years (vv. 9-10). Gog will be buried in the Valley of Hamon-gog, and for seven months the people will bury the dead to cleanse the land, with men appointed to search out every human bone until the land is clean (vv. 11-16).
verseByVerse.theology: God's victory is so complete that the weapons of war become firewood and the land is cleansed of every trace of death.

verseByVerse.quote: "Then those who dwell in the cities of Israel will go out and make fires of the weapons and burn them, shields and bucklers, bow and arrows, clubs and spears; and they will make fires of them for seven years, so that they will not need to take wood out of the field or cut down any out of the forests, for they will make their fires of the weapons. They will seize the spoil of those who despoiled them, and plunder those who plundered them, declares the Lord GOD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Then those who dwell in the cities of Israel will go out and make fires of the weapons and burn them, shields and bucklers, bow and arrows, clubs and spears; and they will make fires of them for seven years,

After the battle, the people of Israel walk out and collect the weapons — shields, bows, arrows, clubs, spears (the ESV notes spears may be "javelins") — and burn them for firewood. And there are so many that they last seven years.

Seven in Scripture often suggests completeness. The picture is of a victory so total that the enemy's entire arsenal becomes fuel for cooking and warmth. Isaiah foresaw the same end of war: they shall beat their swords into plowshares (Isa 2:4). The psalmist: he burns the chariots with fire (Ps 46:9).

so that they will not need to take wood out of the field or cut down any out of the forests, for they will make their fires of the weapons. They will seize the spoil of those who despoiled them, and plunder those who plundered them, declares the Lord GOD.

Plunder those who plundered them. The would-be plunderers of 38:12 are plundered. No weapon that is fashioned against you shall succeed (Isa 54:17).

verseByVerse.quote: "On that day I will give to Gog a place for burial in Israel, the Valley of the Travelers, east of the sea. It will block the travelers, for there Gog and all his multitude will be buried. It will be called the Valley of Hamon-gog. For seven months the house of Israel will be burying them, in order to cleanse the land. All the people of the land will bury them, and it will bring them renown on the day that I show my glory, declares the Lord GOD. They will set apart men to travel through the land regularly and bury those travelers remaining on the face of the land, so as to cleanse it. At the end of seven months they will make their search. And when these travel through the land and anyone sees a human bone, then he shall set up a sign by it, till the buriers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog. (Hamonah is also the name of the city.) Thus shall they cleanse the land.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"On that day I will give to Gog a place for burial in Israel, the Valley of the Travelers, east of the sea. It will block the travelers, for there Gog and all his multitude will be buried. It will be called the Valley of Hamon-gog.

Gog, who wanted to possess the land, gets a piece of it after all: a grave. The ESV notes that Hamon-gog means "the multitude of Gog". The valley will be named after the vast army that lies buried there.

For seven months the house of Israel will be burying them, in order to cleanse the land. All the people of the land will bury them, and it will bring them renown on the day that I show my glory, declares the Lord GOD.

Seven months of burial, in order to cleanse the land. Under the law, anyone who touched a human bone or a grave became unclean (Num 19:16). A land strewn with corpses could not be a holy land. God's victory must be followed by thorough cleansing.

They will set apart men to travel through the land regularly and bury those travelers remaining on the face of the land, so as to cleanse it. At the end of seven months they will make their search. And when these travel through the land and anyone sees a human bone, then he shall set up a sign by it, till the buriers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog. (Hamonah is also the name of the city.) Thus shall they cleanse the land.

The detail is striking. A team is appointed to search the whole land. Anyone who sees even a single bone marks it, and the buriers come. (The ESV notes that At the end may be "Until", and that Hamonah means "multitude".)

Nothing unclean is left. It is a picture of God's thoroughness in purifying his people's world. The new creation will contain no trace of death or defilement: No longer will there be anything accursed (Rev 22:3). And it speaks to the Christian life too: God is not content to win the battle over sin; he cleans up every last bone of it.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: God summons birds and beasts to a great sacrificial feast on the mountains of Israel, to eat the flesh of the mighty and drink the blood of princes (vv. 17-19): And you shall be filled at my table with horses and charioteers, with mighty men and all kinds of warriors (v. 20).
verseByVerse.theology: The proud powers that sought to devour God's people become a feast in God's judgment.

verseByVerse.quote: "As for you, son of man, thus says the Lord GOD: Speak to the birds of every sort and to all beasts of the field: 'Assemble and come, gather from all around to the sacrificial feast that I am preparing for you, a great sacrificial feast on the mountains of Israel, and you shall eat flesh and drink blood. You shall eat the flesh of the mighty, and drink the blood of the princes of the earth—of rams, of lambs, and of he-goats, of bulls, all of them fat beasts of Bashan. And you shall eat fat till you are filled, and drink blood till you are drunk, at the sacrificial feast that I am preparing for you. And you shall be filled at my table with horses and charioteers, with mighty men and all kinds of warriors,' declares the Lord GOD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"As for you, son of man, thus says the Lord GOD: Speak to the birds of every sort and to all beasts of the field: 'Assemble and come, gather from all around to the sacrificial feast that I am preparing for you, a great sacrificial feast on the mountains of Israel, and you shall eat flesh and drink blood.

Now a gruesome invitation. God calls the birds and wild animals to a sacrificial feast. Normally people offered animals as sacrifices. Here the proud warriors are the sacrifice and the animals are the guests.

You shall eat the flesh of the mighty, and drink the blood of the princes of the earth—of rams, of lambs, and of he-goats, of bulls, all of them fat beasts of Bashan. And you shall eat fat till you are filled, and drink blood till you are drunk, at the sacrificial feast that I am preparing for you.

The mighty men and princes are described as sacrificial animals — rams, lambs, goats, bulls. Isaiah used the same shocking image: For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, a great slaughter in the land of Edom (Isa 34:6).

And you shall be filled at my table with horses and charioteers, with mighty men and all kinds of warriors,' declares the Lord GOD.

John saw this very scene at the return of Christ: an angel called to all the birds... "Come, gather for the great supper of God, to eat the flesh of kings, the flesh of captains, the flesh of mighty men, the flesh of horses and their riders" (Rev 19:17-18).

The Bible holds out two suppers. One is the marriage supper of the Lamb (Rev 19:9), to which God's people are invited as guests. The other is the great supper of God, where the proud enemies of God are the meal. Everyone will be at one of them. The invitation to the first is open now.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 21–29 — I Will Not Hide My Face Anymore
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: God will set his glory among the nations, and Israel will know he is the LORD their God (vv. 21-22). The nations will understand that Israel went into exile for its own treachery, when God hid his face (vv. 23-24). Now I will restore the fortunes of Jacob and have mercy on the whole house of Israel (v. 25). They will forget their shame, dwelling securely (vv. 26-28). And I will not hide my face anymore from them, when I pour out my Spirit upon the house of Israel (v. 29).
verseByVerse.theology: The exile had a cause, and its end has a greater cause: God's mercy and the outpouring of his Spirit.

verseByVerse.quote: "And I will set my glory among the nations, and all the nations shall see my judgment that I have executed, and my hand that I have laid on them. The house of Israel shall know that I am the LORD their God, from that day forward. And the nations shall know that the house of Israel went into captivity for their iniquity, because they dealt so treacherously with me that I hid my face from them and gave them into the hand of their adversaries, and they all fell by the sword. I dealt with them according to their uncleanness and their transgressions, and hid my face from them.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"And I will set my glory among the nations, and all the nations shall see my judgment that I have executed, and my hand that I have laid on them.

The house of Israel shall know that I am the LORD their God, from that day forward.

Now the chapter steps back from the battlefield and draws together the whole story of the book. God's glory will be seen by all nations, and Israel will know him from that day forward — no more wavering, no more idols.

And the nations shall know that the house of Israel went into captivity for their iniquity, because they dealt so treacherously with me that I hid my face from them and gave them into the hand of their adversaries, and they all fell by the sword.

I dealt with them according to their uncleanness and their transgressions, and hid my face from them.

Here is an important correction of what the nations thought. They assumed Israel's God had been too weak to protect his people (36:20). Now they will understand: the exile happened for their iniquity. God hid my face from them. It was not weakness but judgment. Israel's God was never defeated; he withdrew his protection from a treacherous people.

That is also true when God's people suffer discipline today. His hiddenness is not absence, and it is not defeat.

verseByVerse.quote: "Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Now I will restore the fortunes of Jacob and have mercy on the whole house of Israel, and I will be jealous for my holy name. They shall forget their shame and all the treachery they have practiced against me, when they dwell securely in their land with none to make them afraid, when I have brought them back from the peoples and gathered them from their enemies' lands, and through them have vindicated my holiness in the sight of many nations. Then they shall know that I am the LORD their God, because I sent them into exile among the nations and then assembled them into their own land. I will leave none of them remaining among the nations anymore. And I will not hide my face anymore from them, when I pour out my Spirit upon the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Now I will restore the fortunes of Jacob and have mercy on the whole house of Israel, and I will be jealous for my holy name.

Now. The word turns the page. The exile had a cause: their sin. The restoration has a cause too: have mercy, and I will be jealous for my holy name. Mercy and God's zeal for his name, the same two themes that run through chapters 20 and 36.

They shall forget their shame and all the treachery they have practiced against me, when they dwell securely in their land with none to make them afraid,

They shall forget their shame. In 16:63 and 36:31 God said they would remember and be ashamed. Both are true in their time. Grace first brings honest shame over sin, and then, in the security of God's love, lifts the shame away. God's forgiven people do not live forever under the weight of what they were.

when I have brought them back from the peoples and gathered them from their enemies' lands, and through them have vindicated my holiness in the sight of many nations. Then they shall know that I am the LORD their God, because I sent them into exile among the nations and then assembled them into their own land. I will leave none of them remaining among the nations anymore.

I will leave none of them remaining. Not one of God's people will be left behind. The Shepherd who seeks the lost (34:16) does not stop until every one is home.

And I will not hide my face anymore from them, when I pour out my Spirit upon the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD."

And the last verse of this section of the book is a wonderful promise. I will not hide my face anymore. The hidden face was the heart of the exile's pain. Now it will never be hidden again.

Why? When I pour out my Spirit upon the house of Israel. Not a few drops, but a pouring out. Joel foresaw the same: I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh (Joel 2:28). And on the day of Pentecost Peter stood up and said that this was happening: in the last days it shall be, God declares, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh (Acts 2:17), and everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved (Acts 2:21).

For everyone who belongs to Christ, God's face is no longer hidden. The Spirit poured out on the church is the pledge that God will never turn his face away from his people again.

39.title: I Will Not Hide My Face Anymore
39.overview:
God declares that he is against Gog and will drive him to the mountains of Israel, strike the weapons from his hands and make him and his armies fall on the open field as food for birds and beasts. Fire will fall on Magog and the coastlands. God will make his holy name known among his people and never let it be profaned again; the day is coming and will surely happen (vv. 1-8).

The people of Israel will burn the enemy's weapons as fuel for seven years and plunder those who plundered them. Gog and his army will be buried in the Valley of Hamon-gog, and for seven months Israel will bury the dead to cleanse the land, appointing men to search out every remaining bone (vv. 9-16).

God invites the birds and beasts to a great sacrificial feast on the mountains of Israel, to eat the flesh of the mighty and drink the blood of princes, filled at his table with horses and warriors (vv. 17-20).

God will set his glory among the nations. Israel will know him from that day on, and the nations will understand that Israel went into exile because of its treachery, when God hid his face. Now God will restore Jacob's fortunes and have mercy on all Israel for the sake of his holy name. They will forget their shame, live securely, and none will be left among the nations. God will never hide his face from them again, when he pours out his Spirit on the house of Israel (vv. 21-29).
39.theology:
God disarms and destroys the final enemies of his people, and the outcome is certain (vv. 1-8; Ps 46:9; Isa 54:17).

God will never again allow his holy name to be profaned (v. 7).

God's victory is followed by thorough cleansing; nothing defiled will remain (vv. 11-16; Num 19:16; Rev 22:3).

The proud enemies of God become the feast of his judgment, while his people are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb (vv. 17-20; Rev 19:17-18).

The exile was God's just judgment, not his weakness; the restoration is his mercy and zeal for his name (vv. 23-25).

Grace first brings honest shame over sin and then lifts it away (v. 26).

God pours out his Spirit and will never hide his face from his people again, fulfilled at Pentecost and in the church (v. 29; Joel 2:28; Acts 2:17, 21).
39.examples:
A bow struck from an archer's hand.

Seven years of firewood from enemy weapons.

A search party marking every bone.

Two suppers: one for the guests, one of the enemies.

A hidden face, and the promise it will never be hidden again.

The Spirit poured out, not sprinkled.

And the side rooms were six cubits on either side.<sup>13</sup>Then he measured the gate from the ceiling of the one side room to the ceiling of the other, a breadth of twenty-five cubits; the openings faced each other.<sup>14</sup>He measured also the vestibule, sixty cubits. And around the vestibule of the gateway was the court.<sup>15</sup>From the front of the gate at the entrance to the front of the inner vestibule of the gate was fifty cubits.<sup>16</sup>And the gateway had windows all around, narrowing inwards toward the side rooms and toward their jambs, and likewise the vestibule had windows all around inside, and on the jambs were palm trees.<sup>17</sup>Then he brought me into the outer court.
