verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The outer east gate is shut: This gate shall remain shut; it shall not be opened, and no one shall enter by it, for the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered by it (vv. 1-2). Only the prince may sit in it to eat bread before the LORD (v. 3).
verseByVerse.theology: The way the LORD has come in is honoured as his alone.

verseByVerse.quote: Then he brought me back to the outer gate of the sanctuary, which faces east. And it was shut. And the LORD said to me, "This gate shall remain shut; it shall not be opened, and no one shall enter by it, for the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered by it. Therefore it shall remain shut. Only the prince may sit in it to eat bread before the LORD. He shall enter by way of the vestibule of the gate, and shall go out by the same way."
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then he brought me back to the outer gate of the sanctuary, which faces east. And it was shut. And the LORD said to me, "This gate shall remain shut; it shall not be opened, and no one shall enter by it, for the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered by it. Therefore it shall remain shut.

In chapter 43 the glory of God came in through the east gate. Now that gate is shut, and it is to stay shut. For the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered by it.

Two things are being said. First, honour: the way the King has walked is his alone. No one else will tread where the glory went. Second, permanence: the glory went out through the east gate once (10:19; 11:23). The shut gate says it will never leave that way again. I will dwell in their midst forever (43:9).

Only the prince may sit in it to eat bread before the LORD. He shall enter by way of the vestibule of the gate, and shall go out by the same way."

One exception: the prince may sit inside the gateway to eat a sacred meal before the LORD, coming in and going out through the vestibule, not the shut doors. Who is he? He is Israel's ruler in the vision, the leader of God's restored people. He is honoured with a place near God's way, but he is clearly a man: later he offers a sin offering for himself (45:22) and has sons (46:16).

So he is not the Messiah himself. But he reminds us of the Messiah's greater glory. Ezekiel's prince eats before the gate the LORD has passed through. Jesus is the LORD who came. Unlike every earthly ruler and priest, He has no need, like those high priests, to offer sacrifices daily, first for his own sins and then for those of the people, since he did this once for all when he offered up himself (Heb 7:27).

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Ezekiel again sees the glory filling the temple and falls on his face (v. 4). God rebukes Israel for bringing foreigners uncircumcised in heart and flesh into his sanctuary (vv. 5-9). The Levites who went astray after idols will bear their punishment: they will guard the gates and do the temple's work, but They shall not come near to me, to serve me as priest (vv. 10-13). Yet I will appoint them to keep charge of the temple (v. 14).
verseByVerse.theology: God takes unfaithfulness in his service seriously, yet still gives the fallen a place to serve.

verseByVerse.quote: Then he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the temple, and I looked, and behold, the glory of the LORD filled the temple of the LORD. And I fell on my face. And the LORD said to me, "Son of man, mark well, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears all that I shall tell you concerning all the statutes of the temple of the LORD and all its laws. And mark well the entrance to the temple and all the exits from the sanctuary. And say to the rebellious house, to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord GOD: O house of Israel, enough of all your abominations, in admitting foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and flesh, to be in my sanctuary, profaning my temple, when you offer to me my food, the fat and the blood. You have broken my covenant, in addition to all your abominations. And you have not kept charge of my holy things, but you have set others to keep my charge for you in my sanctuary.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the temple, and I looked, and behold, the glory of the LORD filled the temple of the LORD. And I fell on my face.

Ezekiel is brought to the front of the temple and sees the glory again, and again he falls on his face. Everything that follows about priests and service is spoken in the light of that glory. Who may serve such a God?

And the LORD said to me, "Son of man, mark well, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears all that I shall tell you concerning all the statutes of the temple of the LORD and all its laws. And mark well the entrance to the temple and all the exits from the sanctuary.

Mark well, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears. Three commands to pay attention. What God says about approaching him is not small print.

And say to the rebellious house, to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord GOD: O house of Israel, enough of all your abominations, in admitting foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and flesh, to be in my sanctuary, profaning my temple, when you offer to me my food, the fat and the blood. You have broken my covenant, in addition to all your abominations.

Enough. God names a specific sin of the old temple: Israel had brought into the sanctuary foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and flesh and let them handle holy things.

Notice the words: uncircumcised in heart and flesh. The problem was not nationality as such. The law had always welcomed the foreigner who joined himself to the LORD. Isaiah promised that God would bring such people to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer (Isa 56:7). The problem was people with no heart for God and no part in his covenant doing the work of worship. And Israel itself could be uncircumcised in heart (Jer 9:26).

And you have not kept charge of my holy things, but you have set others to keep my charge for you in my sanctuary.

Here is the root. God's people, and above all those charged with the sanctuary, had handed their work to others. They wanted the privilege without the responsibility. The warning reaches every church that lets the unconverted lead worship, or every believer who leaves to others what God has given him to guard.

verseByVerse.quote: "Thus says the Lord GOD: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and flesh, of all the foreigners who are among the people of Israel, shall enter my sanctuary. But the Levites who went far from me, going astray from me after their idols when Israel went astray, shall bear their punishment. They shall be ministers in my sanctuary, having oversight at the gates of the temple and ministering in the temple. They shall slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they shall stand before the people, to minister to them. Because they ministered to them before their idols and became a stumbling block of iniquity to the house of Israel, therefore I have sworn concerning them, declares the Lord GOD, and they shall bear their punishment. They shall not come near to me, to serve me as priest, nor come near any of my holy things and the things that are most holy, but they shall bear their shame and the abominations that they have committed. Yet I will appoint them to keep charge of the temple, to do all its service and all that is to be done in it.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Thus says the Lord GOD: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and flesh, of all the foreigners who are among the people of Israel, shall enter my sanctuary.

The door is closed to the uncircumcised heart. In the new covenant this line runs not between nations but between the reborn and the unreborn. For no one is a Jew who is merely one outwardly, nor is circumcision outward and physical. But a Jew is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit (Rom 2:28-29). Through Christ, Gentiles once strangers to the covenants of promise are now fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God (Eph 2:12, 19).

But the Levites who went far from me, going astray from me after their idols when Israel went astray, shall bear their punishment.

Now the Levites — the priestly tribe that served the temple — are judged. Many had followed Israel into idolatry. They shall bear their punishment (the ESV notes this may be "iniquity").

They shall be ministers in my sanctuary, having oversight at the gates of the temple and ministering in the temple. They shall slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they shall stand before the people, to minister to them.

And yet, surprisingly, they are not thrown out. They still have work in God's house: guarding gates, slaughtering sacrifices, serving the people. This is mercy.

Because they ministered to them before their idols and became a stumbling block of iniquity to the house of Israel, therefore I have sworn concerning them, declares the Lord GOD, and they shall bear their punishment. They shall not come near to me, to serve me as priest, nor come near any of my holy things and the things that are most holy, but they shall bear their shame and the abominations that they have committed.

But it is mercy with consequences. Those who led the people into sin — a stumbling block of iniquity — lose the privilege of drawing near as priests. The fact that they misled others makes it more serious. Jesus spoke with the same gravity: whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to sin, it would be better for him to have a great millstone fastened around his neck (Matt 18:6).

Yet I will appoint them to keep charge of the temple, to do all its service and all that is to be done in it.

Yet. Forgiveness does not always remove every consequence of sin; David was forgiven, yet the sword did not depart from his house (2 Sam 12:10, 13). But God still gives the fallen a place and a task. There is humble, useful work in God's house for those who have failed him. That is not a small grace.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 15–27 — The Faithful Sons of Zadok
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who stayed faithful, will come near to minister to God (vv. 15-16). Their clothing, hair, drinking, marriages and contact with the dead are regulated (vv. 17-22, 25-27), and They shall teach my people the difference between the holy and the common, act as judges and keep God's Sabbaths holy (vv. 23-24).
verseByVerse.theology: Faithfulness is honoured with nearness to God, and those who come near must be holy and must teach holiness.

verseByVerse.quote: "But the Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept the charge of my sanctuary when the people of Israel went astray from me, shall come near to me to minister to me. And they shall stand before me to offer me the fat and the blood, declares the Lord GOD. They shall enter my sanctuary, and they shall approach my table, to minister to me, and they shall keep my charge.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"But the Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept the charge of my sanctuary when the people of Israel went astray from me, shall come near to me to minister to me. And they shall stand before me to offer me the fat and the blood, declares the Lord GOD.

In contrast, the sons of Zadok kept faith when everyone else wandered. Zadok had stayed loyal to David and Solomon and was made priest in place of Abiathar (1 Kgs 1:8; 2:35). Long before, God had promised, I will raise up for myself a faithful priest, who shall do according to what is in my heart and in my mind (1 Sam 2:35).

Their reward is nearness: shall come near to me to minister to me. The highest reward of faithfulness is not position or wealth. It is God himself.

They shall enter my sanctuary, and they shall approach my table, to minister to me, and they shall keep my charge.

My table — the same table measured in 41:22. The faithful are brought to God's table. The faithful priest God promised is found finally in Christ, a merciful and faithful high priest in the service of God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people (Heb 2:17). And through him all believers are made a royal priesthood (1 Pet 2:9), invited to draw near.

verseByVerse.quote: When they enter the gates of the inner court, they shall wear linen garments. They shall have nothing of wool on them, while they minister at the gates of the inner court, and within. They shall have linen turbans on their heads, and linen undergarments around their waists. They shall not bind themselves with anything that causes sweat. And when they go out into the outer court to the people, they shall put off the garments in which they have been ministering and lay them in the holy chambers. And they shall put on other garments, lest they transmit holiness to the people with their garments.
verseByVerse.commentary:
When they enter the gates of the inner court, they shall wear linen garments. They shall have nothing of wool on them, while they minister at the gates of the inner court, and within.

The priests must wear linen, as the law had required (Exod 28:39-42): clean, light, white. Nothing of wool.

They shall have linen turbans on their heads, and linen undergarments around their waists. They shall not bind themselves with anything that causes sweat.

Anything that causes sweat. The rule is partly practical: linen keeps the body cool and clean. Some have seen here an echo of the curse, By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread (Gen 3:19) — as if in God's presence the toil of the fall is left behind. Either way, worship is not the sweating labour of people trying to earn God's favour. It is service offered in clean garments God provides.

And when they go out into the outer court to the people, they shall put off the garments in which they have been ministering and lay them in the holy chambers. And they shall put on other garments, lest they transmit holiness to the people with their garments.

The rule of 42:14 is repeated. The holy garments stay in the holy chambers. Holiness is not to be carried out and spread carelessly, as if it were a thing people could catch without meeting God himself.

verseByVerse.quote: They shall not shave their heads or let their locks grow long; they shall surely trim the hair of their heads. No priest shall drink wine when he enters the inner court. They shall not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but only virgins of the offspring of the house of Israel, or a widow who is the widow of a priest.
verseByVerse.commentary:
They shall not shave their heads or let their locks grow long; they shall surely trim the hair of their heads.

No shaved heads, no long unkempt hair: neither the marks of pagan mourning nor neglect. The priest is to look orderly and self-controlled. God's servants do not draw attention to themselves by extremes.

No priest shall drink wine when he enters the inner court.

The same rule God gave Aaron after Nadab and Abihu died for offering unauthorized fire: Drink no wine or strong drink... when you go into the tent of meeting, lest you die (Lev 10:9). Those who handle holy things need clear minds. Be sober-minded; be watchful (1 Pet 5:8).

They shall not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but only virgins of the offspring of the house of Israel, or a widow who is the widow of a priest.

Marriage laws for priests follow Leviticus (Lev 21:7, 13-14), with the added allowance of a priest's widow. The priest's home, not only his work, was to reflect the holiness of his calling. The New Testament asks the same of church leaders: an overseer must manage his own household well (1 Tim 3:4).

verseByVerse.quote: They shall teach my people the difference between the holy and the common, and show them how to distinguish between the unclean and the clean. In a dispute, they shall act as judges, and they shall judge it according to my judgments. They shall keep my laws and my statutes in all my appointed feasts, and they shall keep my Sabbaths holy.
verseByVerse.commentary:
They shall teach my people the difference between the holy and the common, and show them how to distinguish between the unclean and the clean.

Here is the priest's great task, and the reversal of the old failure. Of the priests of Jerusalem God had said: They have made no distinction between the holy and the common, neither have they taught the difference between the unclean and the clean (22:26). Now the faithful priests will do what the unfaithful ones refused.

Teaching is at the heart of ministry. For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and people should seek instruction from his mouth, for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts (Mal 2:7). A church whose leaders no longer teach the difference between holy and common, clean and unclean, has already begun to drift where Jerusalem went.

In a dispute, they shall act as judges, and they shall judge it according to my judgments. They shall keep my laws and my statutes in all my appointed feasts, and they shall keep my Sabbaths holy.

The priests also judge disputes — not by their own opinions but according to my judgments. And they must keep God's feasts and Sabbaths themselves. Those who teach God's law must first obey it.

verseByVerse.quote: They shall not defile themselves by going near to a dead person. However, for father or mother, for son or daughter, for brother or unmarried sister they may defile themselves. After he has become clean, they shall count seven days for him. And on the day that he goes into the Holy Place, into the inner court, to minister in the Holy Place, he shall offer his sin offering, declares the Lord GOD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
They shall not defile themselves by going near to a dead person. However, for father or mother, for son or daughter, for brother or unmarried sister they may defile themselves.

Contact with a corpse made a person ceremonially unclean. Death is the fruit of sin, and the priests of the living God were to keep away from it — except for their closest family (Lev 21:1-3). God does not ask his servants to stop being sons, fathers and brothers. He allows them to grieve.

After he has become clean, they shall count seven days for him. And on the day that he goes into the Holy Place, into the inner court, to minister in the Holy Place, he shall offer his sin offering, declares the Lord GOD.

(The ESV notes that he is a priest.) Even after the normal time of cleansing, the priest waits another seven days, then offers his sin offering before ministering again. The servant of God is never above needing atonement himself.

Christ has changed our relation to death. He entered death and came out of it, so that for believers death no longer defiles but has lost its sting (1 Cor 15:55-57).

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: This shall be their inheritance: I am their inheritance: and you shall give them no possession in Israel; I am their possession (v. 28). They will live from the offerings, the firstfruits and the first of the dough, that a blessing may rest on your house (vv. 29-30), and will not eat what has died or been torn (v. 31).
verseByVerse.theology: The best inheritance is God himself.

verseByVerse.quote: "This shall be their inheritance: I am their inheritance: and you shall give them no possession in Israel; I am their possession. They shall eat the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, and every devoted thing in Israel shall be theirs. And the first of all the firstfruits of all kinds, and every offering of all kinds from all your offerings, shall belong to the priests. You shall also give to the priests the first of your dough, that a blessing may rest on your house. The priests shall not eat of anything, whether bird or beast, that has died of itself or is torn by wild animals.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"This shall be their inheritance: I am their inheritance: and you shall give them no possession in Israel; I am their possession.

Here is the heart of the chapter's promise. The priests receive no land of their own. When the land is divided, they are given a place for their houses (45:4), but no farm, no estate to pass down. Instead: I am their inheritance... I am their possession.

God had said the same to Aaron: I am your portion and your inheritance among the people of Israel (Num 18:20). And David took it on his lips: The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup; you hold my lot (Ps 16:5).

What would you rather have: an estate, or God? The world counts the priests poor. God counts them rich. And every believer, as part of a royal priesthood (1 Pet 2:9), is invited to say the same: My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever (Ps 73:26).

They shall eat the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, and every devoted thing in Israel shall be theirs. And the first of all the firstfruits of all kinds, and every offering of all kinds from all your offerings, shall belong to the priests.

God provides for those who have no land. They live from what the people give to God. So also the Lord commanded that those who proclaim the gospel should get their living by the gospel (1 Cor 9:14).

You shall also give to the priests the first of your dough, that a blessing may rest on your house.

A small, daily gift: the first of the dough, before the family ate (Num 15:20-21). And a promise attached: that a blessing may rest on your house. Giving the first to God is not a loss. Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your produce; then your barns will be filled with plenty (Prov 3:9-10).

The priests shall not eat of anything, whether bird or beast, that has died of itself or is torn by wild animals.

A last rule of holiness, from Lev 22:8: the priests may not eat what has died on its own or been killed by animals. Ezekiel himself had kept this all his life (4:14). Those who live from God's table must not feed on what is unclean.

44.title: I Am Their Inheritance
44.overview:
Ezekiel is brought back to the outer east gate, which is shut. The LORD tells him it must stay shut because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered by it. Only the prince may sit in it to eat bread before the LORD, entering and leaving through the vestibule (vv. 1-3).

At the front of the temple Ezekiel sees the glory of the LORD filling the temple and falls on his face. The LORD tells him to mark well all the temple's statutes and entrances (vv. 4-5).

God rebukes Israel for admitting foreigners uncircumcised in heart and flesh into his sanctuary and for setting others to keep his charge. No such foreigner will enter his sanctuary (vv. 6-9).

The Levites who went astray after idols will bear their punishment. They will guard the gates, slaughter sacrifices and serve the people, but they will not come near to serve as priests or touch the most holy things. Yet God will appoint them to keep charge of the temple (vv. 10-14).

The Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who stayed faithful, will come near to minister to God and approach his table (vv. 15-16).

They must wear linen in the inner court and leave their holy garments in the holy chambers. Their hair, drinking, marriages and contact with the dead are regulated. They are to teach the people the difference between the holy and the common, judge disputes by God's judgments, and keep his feasts and Sabbaths (vv. 17-27).

The priests will have no possession in Israel, for God is their inheritance. They will live from the offerings and firstfruits, and the people's gift of the first of their dough will bring a blessing on their houses. The priests must not eat what has died or been torn (vv. 28-31).
44.theology:
The way by which the LORD has come in is honoured as his alone, and his glory will never depart again (vv. 1-2; 43:9).

Israel's prince is a human ruler who needs atonement; Christ is the sinless Priest-King who offered himself once for all (v. 3; 45:22; Heb 7:26-27).

Worship led by the uncircumcised in heart profanes God's house; in the new covenant, circumcision is of the heart by the Spirit, and Gentiles in Christ are members of God's household (vv. 6-9; Rom 2:28-29; Eph 2:12-19).

Unfaithfulness in God's service has consequences, especially for those who lead others astray, yet God still gives the fallen humble work in his house (vv. 10-14; Matt 18:6; 2 Sam 12:10, 13).

Faithfulness is rewarded with nearness to God, fulfilled in Christ the faithful high priest and shared with his royal priesthood (vv. 15-16; 1 Sam 2:35; Heb 2:17; 1 Pet 2:9).

Those who serve God must be holy in dress, habits and home, and must teach God's people to distinguish holy from common (vv. 17-24; 22:26; Mal 2:7).

God himself is the inheritance of those who serve him (v. 28; Num 18:20; Ps 16:5; 73:26).

God provides for his servants through the gifts of his people, and giving the first to God brings blessing (vv. 29-30; 1 Cor 9:14; Prov 3:9-10).
44.examples:
A gate shut because the King has walked through it.

A prince eating bread before the LORD.

A people who handed God's charge to others.

Fallen Levites still given the gates to keep.

The sons of Zadok, faithful when everyone else wandered.

Linen garments with nothing that causes sweat.

Priests who teach the difference between holy and common.

No land, no estate: "I am their inheritance".

The first of the dough, and a blessing on the house.
